title: Act on a request found in messages
summary: Follow a conversation into the necessary apps and prepare a contextual reply.
prerequisites: Provide the message thread and approved app access; execution requires an agent that can operate those apps.
outcome: The completed bounded task and an unsent reply in context.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Read the messages from [person or thread] and establish exactly what was requested. Check later replies for changes or resolution. Complete the authorized task using [approved applications], verifying the result at the destination. Draft a reply that explains the outcome in the original conversation's tone. Pause before a purchase, booking, deletion, external commitment, or any other irreversible action. If required access is missing, describe the remaining steps precisely instead of claiming completion.

title: Adapt a lesson for three reading levels
summary: Turn a textbook spread into aligned slides, differentiated readings, and a shared assessment.
prerequisites: Textbook page image or PDF, learning standards, and reading-level requirements
Image reading and document/presentation generation
outcome: An 8-10 slide lesson, three reading handouts, and a three-question exit ticket.

steps.title: Build the lesson set
steps.prompt: Use the attached textbook spread, including its diagrams and sidebars, and the supplied learning standard. Create an 8-10 slide lesson with a simplified diagram, three one-page handouts for below-grade, at-grade, and above-grade readers, and a shared three-question exit ticket. Keep the concepts and assessed standard consistent. List vocabulary simplified in the first version. Return editable slide and document files.

steps.title: Add language support
steps.prompt: Adapt the below-grade handout for English learners with a five-term English-Spanish glossary. Replace the final assessment item with a labeled-diagram question that checks the same concept.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Change the teaching sequence
steps.prompt: Rework the deck to begin with observable outcomes before introducing the underlying categories. Use nine slides and preserve alignment to the same standard.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Reuse the lesson rules
steps.prompt: Apply the agreed reading-level rules and assessment structure to [next textbook spread]. Reuse the standards supplied in this conversation and identify any new concepts that require different treatment.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Add an adaptive in-app tour
summary: Guide users through a workflow using semantic targets and real interface state.
prerequisites: Provide the web app, target workflow, documentation, and an environment supporting the chosen browser-agent interface.
outcome: A tested guided flow that explains the interface while users perform the actions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Add a guided tour for [one workflow] in this web app. Inspect its UI, state management, and docs. Expose stable semantic targets and a small tour interface that can highlight or dismiss an explanation, read necessary UI state, and wait for the user to act. Keep guidance tools separate from tools that perform business actions. Preserve authentication and permissions. Reuse existing components and test different starting states, cancellation, and targets that are not yet visible. Return the working flow, verification, and remaining setup without deploying it.

title: Add evaluations to an AI application
summary: Measure real application behavior before changing prompts or model settings.
prerequisites: Provide the application, target behavior, safe fixtures, and a working test endpoint or adapter.
outcome: A runnable evaluation suite with a baseline and explained failures.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Add a Promptfoo evaluation suite for [AI application behavior]. Inspect the actual user-facing code path and existing tests. Propose the smallest useful target adapter, seed cases, assertions, commands, and environment requirements. Exercise the application path where possible, not only an isolated model prompt. Keep fixtures free of secrets and personal customer data. Run and record a baseline before changing production prompts or settings. Deliver a documented local command, passing and failing cases, required setup, and the next coverage worth adding.

title: Add security scanning to a delivery pipeline
summary: Match scan scope to the trigger and handle incomplete runs explicitly.
prerequisites: Provide CI platform, repository, approved scan access, runner constraints, and cost/retention requirements.
outcome: A staged scanning plan and pipeline change with evidence retention and clear enforcement behavior.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Add security scanning to [CI pipeline]. Start with [trigger]: scan the committed merge-base-to-head diff for pull requests, or the full specified revision for default-branch and scheduled runs. Use a trusted runner and isolate secrets from untrusted code. Set practical runtime and estimated cost limits, preserve reports and coverage artifacts, and verify the scanned revision. Begin with review-only reporting; propose blocking thresholds separately. Treat failed or incomplete scans as unresolved, even with no findings. Return a reviewable configuration and evidence from the approved validation run.

title: Adopt Liquid Glass in one iOS flow
summary: Use native visual treatments while preserving a usable fallback.
prerequisites: Requires an iOS app, Xcode 26 or compatible tooling, an iOS 26 simulator, and the chosen flow.
outcome: A focused visual migration with earlier-OS fallback and simulator evidence.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Migrate [high-traffic SwiftUI flow] to native Liquid Glass. Audit existing backgrounds, blur layers, controls, sheets, and toolbars; distinguish interactive chrome from content that should remain plain. Prefer native glass APIs and system controls, keep shapes consistent, and use morphing or interactive effects only where the behavior warrants them. Preserve an availability-gated fallback for earlier supported iOS versions. Build and run the flow in the selected simulator, capture comparison screenshots, and report the scheme, OS, checks, and remaining visual issues.

title: Answer a metric question with a chart
summary: Bring warehouse evidence into a discussion with transparent metric definitions and SQL.
prerequisites: BigQuery or Snowflake read-only access, schema, and metric definitions
Discussion context or a channel export; channel integration for direct replies
outcome: A reproducible chart, the underlying query, and a concise explanation.

steps.title: Chart the metric
steps.prompt: Using [warehouse] and the supplied discussion context, chart weekly signup growth for the previous quarter and investigate the two dips mentioned in the discussion. Show the SQL, date boundaries, timezone, filters, and signup definition. Separate evidence-backed explanations from possibilities requiring more data. If no warehouse is connected, provide the query and identify the result data needed.

steps.title: Correct the definition
steps.prompt: Apply this corrected metric definition: [definition]. Recalculate the chart and describe how the correction changes the result. Write an explicit reusable channel instruction; persist it only if the channel supports that capability.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the daily metric routine
steps.prompt: Define a weekday 8 a.m. routine in [timezone] that posts the previous day's agreed metrics and a two-line anomaly summary. Check which routines already exist before creating one, and state any missing scheduling or channel capability.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Analyze channel requests instead
steps.prompt: Using the supplied channel history, chart weekly request volume and time to first reply. State how requests, threads, unanswered items, and missing timestamps are counted.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Answer an ad-hoc business data question
summary: Turn a stakeholder question into traceable SQL, an explanation, and a reusable chart.
prerequisites: Business question, warehouse schema or dbt models, metric definitions, and data dictionary
Read-only warehouse connection, or exported data for local analysis
outcome: A validated query, result table, driver analysis, and dashboard specification.

steps.title: Investigate the question
steps.prompt: Investigate this business question: [for example, why did gross margin decline in EMEA this quarter?]. Use the supplied schema and certified metric definitions to write SQL, explain its joins and filters, and run it only if a read-only warehouse connection is available. Otherwise provide the query and identify the missing results. Analyze supported drivers and supply a chart specification that makes the answer reusable in our dashboard.

steps.title: Document the query workflow
steps.prompt: Capture the metric definitions, query checks, naming conventions, and answer format as reusable instructions for similar stakeholder questions.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare incoming-question triage
steps.prompt: Define a workflow for reviewing new requests in [analytics channel], saving the query and draft response for each thread, and holding the answer for my review. Specify the required channel and warehouse permissions before any hourly automation is created.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Assemble a consistent offer package
summary: Keep the offer document, candidate email, and call presentation aligned with approved terms.
prerequisites: Attach the candidate summary, offer template, compensation approval, and benefits overview.
Document and HTML generation are required; connect Drive or Microsoft 365 if the inputs live there.
outcome: A review-ready offer, warm email draft, and short HTML call deck.

steps.title: Build the package
steps.prompt: Prepare the offer materials for [candidate and role] from these approved sources. Complete the offer template, draft an email inviting the candidate to the offer conversation, and create a short HTML presentation covering responsibilities, compensation, benefits, and specific reasons we want them. Keep the title, amounts, and start date consistent across all three, flag missing approvals, and leave everything for my review.

steps.title: Check the terms
steps.prompt: Audit the three outputs against the compensation approval and benefits document. Show any mismatch or unsupported claim, correct it across every artifact, and give me a short checklist for the offer call.

title: Assemble a design specification from scattered decisions
summary: Reconcile conversation threads, notes, and screenshots into one reviewable spec.
prerequisites: Design threads, meeting notes, screenshots, and project documents
Slack and Notion access or exported material
outcome: A source-linked specification with contradictions and changed decisions made explicit.

steps.title: Assemble the specification
steps.prompt: Combine the supplied project threads, notes, and screenshots into a design spec with problem, goals, constraints, proposed solution, open questions, and out-of-scope work. Cite the source and date for decisions already made. Flag contradictions, distinguish proposals from decisions, and avoid resolving disputed requirements without evidence.

steps.title: Save the specification format
steps.prompt: Create reusable instructions for the section order, evidence links, decision log, and contradiction flags. Incorporate the review feedback into the template.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Highlight decision changes
steps.prompt: Update the spec from new source material and add a concise top section listing decisions changed since the previous version, with supporting references.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the review refresh
steps.prompt: Define an 8 a.m. weekday refresh from [project channel and folder] that updates the spec and identifies overnight changes. Specify source and scheduling access before enabling a recurring run.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Assemble a launch campaign kit
summary: Coordinate first drafts across customer, internal, social, and creative channels.
prerequisites: Provide launch plan, product evidence, creative brief, assets, page links, and approval guidance.
outcome: A coordinated campaign draft pack with claim and asset review flags.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Create the first campaign kit for [launch] from the supplied plan, product notes, tracker, creative brief, page links, and approval rules. Include a launch-review brief, customer email, internal announcement, social post, two-week content calendar, creative or agency brief, staging-page fixes, and a team update. Keep the central message and facts consistent across formats. Flag unsupported claims, missing assets, and product or legal approval needs. Do not send or publish any draft.

steps.title: Check launch readiness
steps.prompt: Review the kit for inconsistent dates or claims, missing assets, broken handoffs, and unresolved approvals. Prioritize the gaps that would block launch and identify the owner where documented.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Assess exposure to a dependency advisory
summary: Determine whether a public package incident actually affects your repository.
prerequisites: Provide the advisory URL, repository, lockfiles, and relevant CI or build configuration.
outcome: An exposure assessment with repository evidence and a proposed remediation path.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Evaluate [public package advisory] against this repository using read-only inspection. Establish affected packages and versions from authoritative sources. Inspect manifests, lockfiles, CI permissions, lifecycle scripts, and relevant built or vendored artifacts. Explain what proves exposure and what would rule it out, including token or cache implications when relevant. Classify the result as confirmed, unresolved, or ruled out, with file references and impact limits. Do not install packages, execute lifecycle scripts, rotate credentials, or delete files.

steps.title: Plan remediation
steps.prompt: For confirmed exposure, propose the exact package or configuration changes, verification, rollback, and any credential review required. Keep commands that execute untrusted code out of the plan unless their safety is established.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Assess security across a repository portfolio
summary: Keep each repository's revision, findings, and coverage independently traceable.
prerequisites: Provide authorized repository URLs, full commit SHAs, scan tooling, and approved concurrency and cost limits.
outcome: A per-repository assessment ledger with separate evidence and follow-up actions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prepare and run an authorized security assessment for [repository inventory]. Require a unique ID and full commit SHA for every repository; do not silently substitute a branch tip or uncommitted state. Use the approved concurrency, scan mode, and estimated cost limits. Save private results separately for each repository outside the scanned trees. Verify the scanned revisions, completion status, findings, and coverage gaps. Distinguish successful execution from an absence of vulnerabilities. Return a portfolio ledger of investigations, accepted fixes, and incomplete coverage, with the evidence paths and safe resume instructions.

title: Audit a course before refreshing it
summary: Find outdated content, alignment gaps, and overloaded weeks.
prerequisites: Provide syllabus, slides, readings, assignments, rubrics, outcomes, course notes, and term calendar.
outcome: A prioritized course-refresh plan tied to the source materials.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review [course] as a connected teaching system. Compare its syllabus, slides, readings, assignments, rubrics, outcomes, and calendar. Identify stale examples, duplicate content, gaps between learning outcomes and assessment, contradictory student instructions, and unusually heavy weeks. Rank proposed improvements by educational impact and effort, citing the evidence for each. Explain dependencies between changes so one revision does not break another component. Return the refresh plan before editing source files.

title: Audit a manual workflow
summary: Find the bottlenecks and define two narrow automation opportunities.
prerequisites: Provide tracker, process documentation, handoff notes, tickets, metrics, and operational constraints.
outcome: A workflow audit, revised process draft, and two focused automation specifications.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Audit [workflow] before [deadline]. Reconstruct its steps and owners from the tracker, documentation, handoff notes, tickets, metrics, and discussions. Identify stuck points, repeated questions, missing data, and conflicting or stale instructions. Draft an updated process description and a small automation specification for the two most repetitive manual steps. Explain inputs, outputs, exceptions, and human decisions. Keep recommendations bounded and do not implement or publish process changes.

steps.title: Select the first automation
steps.prompt: Compare the two automation candidates by frequency, effort, dependencies, failure impact, and available evidence. Recommend the smallest useful first release and define how to verify that it helps.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Audit competitor flows with a shared heuristic rubric
summary: Score real screens against consistent usability principles and record the evidence.
prerequisites: Competitor and internal screenshots or accessible flows
Nielsen's ten heuristics, three custom criteria, and a severity/scoring scale
outcome: A comparative scorecard with useful patterns and avoidable mistakes.

steps.title: Build the heuristic scorecard
steps.prompt: Audit the supplied competitor flows against Nielsen's ten heuristics and [our three custom criteria]. Use the same scoring scale for every screen and record screenshot-level evidence for each finding. Compare strengths and weaknesses with our equivalent flow. Finish with three patterns worth adapting and three mistakes to avoid; identify interactions that static screenshots cannot establish.

steps.title: Refine the rubric
steps.prompt: Incorporate my feedback into the criteria, severity scale, and evidence standard. Create reusable review instructions with examples of how to score ambiguous cases.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Show the changes
steps.prompt: Compare this scorecard with last quarter's version. Highlight changed scores and explain whether the product changed, the evidence improved, or the rubric changed.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare release monitoring
steps.prompt: Define a Monday 10 a.m. review of new screenshots in [teardown folder]. Re-score affected flows and flag criteria where competitors now perform better. State the source and scheduling access needed for ongoing monitoring.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Audit consistency across course sections
summary: Separate required alignment from legitimate instructor choices.
prerequisites: Provide section syllabi, assignments, schedules, outcomes, LMS exports, and department guidance.
outcome: A faculty review checklist of evidence-backed inconsistencies and priorities.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Compare the supplied sections of [course]. Check syllabi, assessment requirements, schedules, outcomes, and student instructions against department guidance. Distinguish required common standards from areas where instructors have discretion. Identify student-facing conflicts, cite the source for each, and rank them by urgency and impact. Propose a baseline alignment checklist and responsible owners where documented. Return the audit for faculty review and leave the source materials unchanged.

title: Audit existing interface patterns before designing
summary: Find comparable components across the product and decide which one is worth reusing.
prerequisites: Connect Figma and GitHub, or provide design-system exports, screenshots, and ownership records.
Amplitude access is optional for engagement evidence; include a screenshot of the destination surface.
outcome: A side-by-side pattern inventory with ownership, evidence, and a reuse recommendation.

steps.title: Find the precedent
steps.prompt: Before designing [pattern] for [surface], locate existing variants in our design files and codebase, including [related names or forms]. For each, provide a screenshot or design link, implementation reference, owner, and relevant usage evidence if available. Recommend the best fit for the destination and explain any gaps in the evidence.

steps.title: Plan consolidation
steps.prompt: Show how to adapt the recommended pattern to the destination. Identify other surfaces that would benefit from adopting it, the owners to involve, and compatibility or accessibility checks needed before consolidation.

title: Audit renewal risk across your account book
summary: Explain account risk using usage trends, customer sentiment, and outstanding commitments.
prerequisites: Connect Salesforce and Gong, or attach renewal, usage, and call-note exports.
Provide your risk rubric and open executive commitments; Zendesk is optional for support context.
Interactive artifact support is needed for a filterable view.
outcome: A filterable renewal-risk table with evidence and targeted save actions.

steps.title: Score the renewal book
steps.prompt: Review accounts renewing within [90 days]. Use our rubric to assign red, yellow, or green risk from usage trends, recent customer sentiment, and unfulfilled commitments. Cite the signals driving each score, show missing data, and include renewal date, value, owner, and segment. Build a leadership view filterable by owner, segment, and risk.

steps.title: Act on new risks
steps.prompt: Compare with the previous audit. For every account newly red, explain what changed and propose the next action with its owner. Separate new deterioration from newly available evidence, and refresh the existing risk view.

title: Audit visual assets against brand rules
summary: Check image exports for outdated logos, incorrect colors, and missing required copy.
prerequisites: Brand guidelines, required legal copy, and PNG/JPEG asset files
Image inspection; optional live asset URLs, browser access, and Asana connection
outcome: An asset-level compliance report grouped by issue and confidence.

steps.title: Audit the asset folder
steps.prompt: Inspect every supplied PNG and JPEG against [brand guidelines] and [required-copy document]. Check logo versions, specified colors, and the presence and readable size of required copy. Group findings by violation type. For each, report filename, expected rule, observed value, evidence, and confidence. Separate uncertain visual estimates from exact file metadata and count assets with no detected issues.

steps.title: Check published versions
steps.prompt: Use [asset URL mapping] to inspect the live page for each high-confidence finding. Report whether the published asset still shows the issue or appears corrected; identify pages you cannot access.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare correction tasks
steps.prompt: Prepare one Asana task per high-confidence issue with the asset owner, filename, relevant rule, and proposed correction. Create tasks only when the project and write access are available.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Repeat the audit
steps.prompt: Write reusable brand-audit instructions and a Friday 2 p.m. schedule specification in [timezone], including the asset location and summary destination. Configure the recurring run only if the necessary file, scheduling, and messaging connections are available.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Benchmark a protein-folding hypothesis
summary: Run controlled architecture experiments with durable records and comparable results.
prerequisites: Provide the model repository, NanoFold benchmark setup, scoring command, and compute limits.
outcome: An experiment log with matched metrics, resource costs, and defensible conclusions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Evaluate whether sparse higher-order geometric states improve this AlphaFold2-style model on NanoFold. Keep the usual MSA and residue-pair representations; investigate learned triplet faces and quadruplet tetrahedra using only official inputs and geometry recycled by the model. Track the strategy, experiments, and observations in durable files. For each iteration, state the hypothesis, make a bounded change, run the relevant tests and matched benchmark, and record lDDT-C-alpha, latency, memory, and failure modes. Decide whether to keep or revise the change. Do not present a smoke test or single-chain overfit as evidence of generalization.

title: Bookend your day with a briefing and a wrap
summary: Start with priorities and finish by carrying unresolved work into tomorrow.
prerequisites: Connect your calendar, email, chat, and task tools, or attach current exports.
Use a writable Daily folder for dated notes; recurring runs require scheduling support.
outcome: A dated daily note connecting morning intentions to evening outcomes.

steps.title: Start the day
steps.prompt: Read my calendar, outstanding tasks, relevant messages, and yesterday's daily note. Write a briefing shorter than one page: urgent problems, deadlines, people waiting for me, and my three best next actions. Explain the priority order and link supporting items. Save it as the morning section of Daily/[today].md.

steps.title: Close the day
steps.prompt: Compare today's activity with the morning plan. Append an evening section to the same note covering completed work, deferred items and reasons, unresolved dependencies, and tomorrow's first action. Carry forward unfinished commitments explicitly.

title: Bring order to your Google Drive
summary: Create a sensible folder structure and separate uncertain, duplicate, and outdated files for review.
prerequisites: Requires browser control signed into Google Drive or an equivalent Drive integration with file-management access.
Choose the folders in scope and list naming conventions and items to preserve.
outcome: An organized Drive with a movement log and a review queue.

steps.title: Plan and organize
steps.prompt: Review [Drive folders] and propose a structure based on projects, contents, and dates. Show the folders you would create and any ambiguous files before moving anything. After I approve, move only files we can manage, record old and new locations, and list shared files whose ownership prevents changes. Flag suspected duplicates and stale documents separately.

steps.title: Refine the cleanup
steps.prompt: Suggest descriptive names for generically named files and identify archive candidates using [date rule]. For suspected duplicates, compare contents and versions rather than relying on filenames. Show the proposed changes and which copy would be retained before any deletion.

title: Build a board narrative from scattered evidence
summary: Follow a project tracker into connected sources and reconcile the numbers before shaping the story.
prerequisites: Provide a project tracker and the previous board deck; connect Slack, email, and Drive.
Requires browser access to live dashboards plus PowerPoint, Excel, and Word creation.
outcome: A decision-focused deck, supporting workbook, and executive pre-read.

steps.title: Follow the evidence
steps.prompt: Prepare a board discussion on [decision]. Start with [project tracker], follow referenced people, conversations, documents, and metrics, then compare conflicting figures with the authoritative systems. Explain scope and timing differences instead of simply choosing the newest number. Create a 12-to-15-slide PowerPoint with notes, an Excel evidence appendix, and a two-page Word brief built around the conclusion the evidence supports.

steps.title: Challenge the story
steps.prompt: Identify the three hardest board questions and the weakest links in the argument. Add evidence-linked responses to the speaker notes, retain unresolved disagreements in the appendix, and cut the deck to [slide count] while preserving the reasoning.

title: Build a cited discovery chronology
summary: Connect documents over time to identify patterns, contradictions, and evidence worth investigating.
prerequisites: Provide discovery materials and their document index, or connect Gmail and Drive where they are stored.
Specify the dispute, relevant period, issues, and firm memo format.
outcome: A legal chronology and a memo with traceable findings and witness leads.

steps.title: Map the record
steps.prompt: Review the supplied discovery for [dispute]. Build a chronological table with document IDs, dates, participants, event descriptions, and precise citations. Analyze patterns in scope changes, deliverables, communication, and billing, including evidence that cuts against our position. Draft a memo distinguishing facts, inferences, unresolved contradictions, and potential witness leads.

steps.title: Investigate a contradiction
steps.prompt: For [issue or milestone], gather all related contemporaneous communications and compare them with later claims. Present exact source locations for important passages, identify missing links, and condense the strongest supported points and next investigative steps into a one-page counsel brief.

title: Build a competitive battlecard library
summary: Combine lost-deal evidence with current competitor research into usable sales guidance.
prerequisites: Closed-lost deal notes with competitor fields for a defined period
CRM export or connection, web research access, and optional brand reference
outcome: A searchable competitor dashboard with grounded objections and talk tracks.

steps.title: Create the battlecards
steps.prompt: Review closed-lost deals from the last six months for [competitors]. Identify loss patterns in the deal notes, then research current competitor sites, reviews, and positioning. Build a compact interactive dashboard with a competitor list and detailed battlecards containing strengths, weaknesses, differentiators, objection responses, and cited evidence. Date time-sensitive claims and distinguish customer perceptions from verified product facts.

steps.title: Practice realistic objections
steps.prompt: Create three sales-call exercises from actual objections in the losses to [competitor]. Include the objection, an evidence-backed response, and likely follow-up questions.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Update earlier positioning
steps.prompt: Compare the current evidence for [competitor] with our previous-quarter battlecard. Explain what changed and propose precise updates to the counter-messaging.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Build a consistent performance-review workflow
summary: Give managers the same evidence-gathering process, rating definitions, and review template.
prerequisites: Attach the performance framework, rating definitions, review template, and cycle instructions.
Gusto and Drive can supply the roster and documents; Asana can supply cycle deadlines.
Requires custom-skill support to install the reusable workflow.
outcome: A reusable manager workflow grounded in the approved performance framework.

steps.title: Create the manager workflow
steps.prompt: Build a performance-review skill using our current cycle materials. Guide managers through collecting evidence, mapping it to the approved competencies, proposing ratings against the exact supplied definitions, and drafting in our template. Do not introduce extra criteria. Keep evidence gaps visible and require the manager to own and confirm the assessment.

steps.title: Check consistency
steps.prompt: Run the workflow on these sample review notes. Highlight unsupported ratings, inconsistent interpretations of the same competency, and missing examples. Improve the instructions so managers receive the same prompts and calibration guidance without inventing employee evidence.

title: Build a creative request workspace
summary: Connect complete briefs, review feedback, and final assets in one process.
prerequisites: Provide the brief template, brand resources, approved request data, requester/reviewer roles, and authenticated app environment.
outcome: A private request app with persistent records and tested role-based access.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build a creative request app for [team] using its approved brief template. Capture audience, message, format, requested date, reviewer, and reference links; keep the requested date distinct from the team's agreed delivery date. Give each request its brief, owner, status, current draft, feedback, and final asset, using New, In progress, In review, and Delivered. Add filters for owner, status, and agreed date. Require sign-in; enforce requester access to their own records and creative-team management rights on the server. Save feedback across visits. Test validation, status changes, reloads, and direct cross-requester access. Keep source files linked and show a private reviewed preview before publishing.

steps.title: Review the queue
steps.prompt: Identify overdue work, unassigned requests, missing delivery agreements, and feedback awaiting action. Show the evidence and suggested next step for each without changing status or contacting people.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Build a distinctive professional portfolio
summary: Turn career material and design references into a working personal website.
prerequisites: Resume, detailed project descriptions, achievements, and visual references
A local coding/browser environment; hosting access only if publishing is requested
outcome: A responsive portfolio with project stories and a clear publication path.

steps.title: Build the portfolio
steps.prompt: Create a responsive portfolio from my attached resume, project descriptions, and visual references. Use an editorial visual direction with purposeful typography, asymmetry, and carefully chosen details. Present only supported accomplishments and distinguish missing content from finished copy. Deliver working HTML and assets, then explain a beginner-friendly path to publishing them.

steps.title: Publish with the available host
steps.prompt: Use the configured hosting connection, such as Netlify, to create and publish this portfolio to [destination]. If hosting is not connected, provide exact manual steps. Report a live URL only after a deployment succeeds, and explain how to update it.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Refine the motion
steps.prompt: Add subtle project hover states and short heading reveals that support navigation. Preserve keyboard accessibility and reduced-motion behavior.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Develop one case study
steps.prompt: Expand [project] into a full case study covering the problem, research, process, iterations, challenges, solution, and measured impact. Use my source material and mark missing evidence instead of fabricating results.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Build a financial variance bridge
summary: Reconcile major movements into drivers that owners can confirm.
prerequisites: Provide current and comparison workbooks, operating metrics, owner notes, and a materiality threshold.
outcome: An editable driver bridge with source references and unresolved explanations.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Explain the [period] change between [actuals, budget, or forecast versions]. Build a formula-based bridge across the relevant revenue, margin, operating-expense, EBITDA, cash-flow, or balance-sheet lines. Rank drivers by their contribution, reconcile differences between source files, and link each explanation to its workbook tab or owner note. Show items below [materiality threshold] separately. Label unsupported causes as hypotheses and draft the questions needed to confirm them. Preserve the original inputs.

steps.title: Challenge the bridge
steps.prompt: Review the largest drivers for double-counting, unexplained residuals, and unsupported causality. Reconcile the bridge back to the total movement and list finance-owner confirmations still needed.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Build a first-week onboarding portal
summary: Guide new hires through sourced tasks while keeping individual progress private.
prerequisites: Provide the approved first-week plan, resources, contacts, practice task, and an authenticated app environment.
outcome: A private portal with persistent checklists, practice instructions, and verified progress isolation.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build an onboarding portal for [role] from the approved first-week plan. Include daily tasks, resources, contacts, and the end-of-week practice task. Show each task's purpose, completion criteria, source link, and support contact; use time estimates only when supplied. Preserve the plan's sequence and add progress and resume controls. title: Compare alternative budget futures
summary: See how a funding change affects both spending amounts and the balance between programs.
prerequisites: Provide total budget, category amounts or percentages, funding changes, and fixed-cost constraints.
Requires interactive visualization support for controls and scenario toggles.
outcome: An interactive scenario comparison with explicit constraints and board talking points.

steps.title: Show the scenarios
steps.prompt: Our current budget is [total], split across [categories and shares]. Compare loss of [funding], no change, and growth of [amount]. Draw aligned stacked bars with a toggle between currency and percentages. State the allocation assumptions, identify which categories absorb pressure, and give each scenario a one-sentence operational interpretation.

steps.title: Apply a constraint
steps.prompt: Hold [category] at its present amount and recalculate the funding-loss scenario. Show where the remaining reductions fall, then compare an immediate loss with a two-year phase-out. Rewrite the board talking point to reflect the actual tradeoff.

title: Compare business growth with economic indicators
summary: Combine revenue from board decks with matching public macroeconomic series.
prerequisites: Quarterly board decks with revenue figures
Access to FRED data or downloaded series; chart and presentation generation
outcome: A sourced comparison chart, short interpretation, and board slide.

steps.title: Build the comparison
steps.prompt: Extract revenue for [four quarters] from the supplied board decks and record the slide supporting each figure. Retrieve matching GDP growth and inflation series from FRED, noting units, frequency, and release dates. Compare our revenue growth with these indicators using aligned periods and clearly labeled axes. Create a chart and concise interpretation without treating correlation as causation.

steps.title: Add more indicators
steps.prompt: Add unemployment and consumer-confidence measures for the same period. Choose a presentation that remains readable despite differing units and explain any series transformation.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Extend the history
steps.prompt: Use the additional archived board decks to extend the comparison to three years. Check that revenue definitions and macroeconomic frequencies remain comparable.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Create a board slide
steps.prompt: Create a single PowerPoint slide with the chart, key figures, source notes, and three useful discussion points. Return it as an editable file.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Compare campaign spending and lead generation
summary: Use consistent filters and weighted calculations to explain campaign performance.
prerequisites: Provide campaign-by-week data, reporting period, currency, time zone, lead definition, and attribution rules.
outcome: A validated dashboard with source-row drilldown and an explicit refresh process.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build a private campaign dashboard from [file or exact sheet tab]. Inspect row counts, dates, campaign IDs, duplicates, currencies, missing values, and mapping gaps first. Show spend, leads, cost per lead, weekly trends, and campaign comparisons using the same filtered rows throughout. Compute cost per lead as total spend divided by total leads, not an average of row ratios; use N/A for zero leads. Keep missing values distinct from zero and currencies separate without an approved conversion rule. Include source-row drilldown and a safe export-refresh process. Validate totals, filters, duplicates, partial weeks, and mobile layout. Do not infer revenue or lead quality from lead counts.

steps.title: Compare consecutive periods
steps.prompt: Compare [two periods] using consistent definitions and complete-week boundaries. Explain which campaigns drove changes in spend, leads, and aggregate cost per lead, and flag data coverage that limits the comparison.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Compare drug-target evidence
summary: Rank biological targets across independent research evidence streams.
prerequisites: Provide the disease, candidate targets, and access to relevant genetics, expression, literature, and clinical sources.
outcome: A target-by-evidence matrix, ranked hypotheses, and explicit confidence limits.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Compare TSLP, IL33, and IL1RL1 as research targets for asthma. Review independent evidence from human genetics, cohort replication and PheWAS, disease associations, clinical precedent, literature, and tissue or cell-type expression. Score each target from 1 to 5 within each evidence stream using stated criteria. Separate direct asthma findings from related allergic conditions. Reconcile conflicting evidence and provide the overall ranking, confidence, and key limitations. Include a prioritization heatmap and a sourced summary of lead asthma-associated variants. Keep this a research prioritization exercise, not a treatment recommendation.

title: Compare grants by opportunity and effort
summary: See award size, uncertainty, deadline, and preparation load together before choosing what to pursue.
prerequisites: Provide your grant pipeline with awards, deadlines, effort estimates, and success-rate evidence where available.
Requires interactive visualization and current official-program research for deadlines and eligibility.
outcome: An explorable grant comparison and a realistic submission schedule.

steps.title: Map the grant choices
steps.prompt: Compare these grant opportunities across award amount, estimated chance, deadline, eligibility, and effort. Build a linked chart and table with filters, flag near-term deadlines, and verify current requirements on official pages. Label uncertain success estimates and omit expected-value calculations where the inputs are unsupported. Help me shortlist options under [capacity constraint].

steps.title: Work back from deadlines
steps.prompt: For the shortlisted grants due within [90 days], build a submission timeline working backward from verified deadlines, including partner input and internal review. Mark [submitted grant] as in progress and reprioritize the remaining workload without losing its follow-up obligations.

title: Compare preclinical study designs
summary: Bring experimental designs and source records together into a traceable cross-study comparison.
prerequisites: Requires Benchling or an equivalent research-data connection with access to the selected studies, protocols, and lab notebooks.
Specify study IDs and the intended report format.
outcome: A referenced comparison table and draft study report.

steps.title: Compare the studies
steps.prompt: Retrieve [study A] and [study B] from our research platform. Compare objectives, model systems, sample sizes, test articles, dosing, collection times, endpoints, and analytical methods. Link every supporting notebook and protocol, identify missing details, and explain which design differences limit direct comparison of results.

steps.title: Draft the report
steps.prompt: Use the verified comparison and underlying results to draft a study report in [required structure]. Keep methods, observations, interpretation, and limitations distinct. Preserve source links and flag unresolved discrepancies for scientific review before the report is used in a submission.

title: Compare products across retailer sites
summary: Normalize product specifications and current offers into one useful shortlist.
prerequisites: Product-page URLs or accessible browser tabs and the criteria that matter
Web or browser access; document connection only for saving directly to an online document
outcome: A sourced comparison table with category winners and buying considerations.

steps.title: Compare the products
steps.prompt: Compare the products at [URLs]. For laptops, prioritize processor, RAM, storage, screen, battery claims, and weight; use [my priorities] for another category. Normalize units and exact model configurations in a side-by-side table. Link each source, note when it was checked, and identify the strongest option per criterion without inventing missing specifications.

steps.title: Add another option
steps.prompt: Add [new product URL] using the same specification and pricing definitions. Update category winners and explain whether the additional option changes the shortlist.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Check recurring review concerns
steps.prompt: Research reviews of [leading option]. Summarize repeated strengths and complaints, separating independent testing from seller claims and isolated anecdotes.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Compare current prices
steps.prompt: Find current offers for the exact selected configuration in [country]. Compare total cost, availability, delivery, and warranty terms rather than only the headline price.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Compare strategic scenarios and tradeoffs
summary: Make costs, timing, risk, and assumptions comparable across options.
prerequisites: Provide the decision, financial model, operational context, stakeholder input, and evaluation criteria.
outcome: A scenario model and recommendation with visible assumptions and sensitivities.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Compare the strategic options for [decision] using [criteria] and the supplied model and planning evidence. Build a prioritization matrix covering cost, timing, customer or business impact, dependencies, risks, mitigation, and ownership. Make assumptions visible and distinguish supported estimates from inputs requiring approval. Recommend a path and explain what is sacrificed relative to the alternatives. Work on a separate model so the original remains intact.

steps.title: Test sensitivity
steps.prompt: Vary [high-impact assumptions] across plausible ranges. Show when the preferred option changes and which uncertain input is most valuable to resolve before deciding.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Compare travel destinations side by side
summary: Research realistic options for your dates and make the tradeoffs visible in a polished workbook.
prerequisites: Specify destinations, origin, dates, trip length, budget, and travel preferences.
Requires current web research and spreadsheet generation with image and formatting support.
outcome: A visual destination comparison with cited facts and adjustable preference weights.

steps.title: Research the options
steps.prompt: Compare [destinations] for a [length]-day trip from [origin] in [month]. Build a spreadsheet showing all options together across transport, typical costs, weather, food, culture, activities, and practical constraints. Cite current sources and official tourism links, explain subjective ratings, and use compact thumbnails, heatmaps, and readable column widths. Label cost estimates with their dates.

steps.title: Weight the decision
steps.prompt: Add editable weights emphasizing [priorities] and recalculate the comparison transparently. For the leading option, draft a realistic itinerary with travel time, approximate costs, and current booking links; keep uncertain prices and availability visible.

title: Compare vendor proposals on equal terms
summary: Normalize differently structured offers into a clear commercial decision.
prerequisites: Vendor proposals, required features, team size, and decision criteria
Spreadsheet and document generation
outcome: A side-by-side workbook, negotiation questions, and decision memo.

steps.title: Normalize the proposals
steps.prompt: Compare the attached proposals for [service]. Extract base charges, per-user and add-on fees, implementation timing, contract length, renewal and exit terms, feature coverage, and support. Build a polished comparison workbook with consistent units and source references. Highlight hidden costs, ambiguous terms, and material gaps; do not treat an unstated feature as included.

steps.title: Draft the decision memo
steps.prompt: Recommend a vendor against our stated priorities. Explain cost, fit, tradeoffs, unresolved questions, and the terms we should negotiate before committing.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare vendor questions
steps.prompt: Create a separate call-question list for each vendor, focused on ambiguous terms, optional charges, implementation dependencies, and missing capabilities.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Model the pricing crossover
steps.prompt: Compare the flat-rate and per-employee offers across [20-50] employees. Show the break-even calculation and a total-cost chart including applicable fixed and variable fees.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Complete a task across desktop apps
summary: Use visible applications and local files to finish a clearly bounded task.
prerequisites: Requires a desktop agent with computer-control access and the relevant apps signed in.
outcome: A completed task or a precise account of the remaining manual steps.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Help me complete [task] using [approved applications or folders]. Inspect the current screen and relevant files before acting. Follow the task across the necessary apps, verify the result in each destination, and summarize what changed. Ask before sending anything, making a purchase, confirming a booking, deleting data, or making another consequential change. If computer-control access is unavailable, tell me which steps I need to perform instead of claiming you completed them.

title: Configure automatic pull-request security reviews
summary: Choose review triggers and reporting thresholds suited to repository risk.
prerequisites: Provide repository access, supported security-review tooling, and current configuration documentation.
outcome: A review configuration proposal with sensitive-path overrides and a validation plan.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review the security-review options for [repository] using its current tooling documentation. Propose when automatic and manually requested reviews should run, which severity levels should be reported, and which sensitive paths need tighter thresholds. Consider authentication, authorization, payment, infrastructure, and dependency code separately from low-risk areas. Explain the difference between ordinary correctness review and security analysis. Show the proposed settings, expected pull-request output, and a controlled verification change before altering repository configuration.

title: Connect biotech evidence with financial downside
summary: Cross-check filings, trial design, and patent documents before modeling a pipeline valuation.
prerequisites: Company filings, clinical-trial protocol, patent documents, and stated management guidance
Spreadsheet generation; no external estimates unless separately supplied
outcome: A document-grounded research memo and transparent scenario workbook.

steps.title: Evaluate the evidence together
steps.prompt: Evaluate [biotech company] ahead of [clinical milestone] using only the attached filings, trial protocol, and patent documents. Assess the science and trial design, map supported pipeline-valuation inputs, and identify contradictions with management's narrative. Model downside scenarios where the documents support inputs; leave unsupported values explicitly unresolved. Produce a research memo and downloadable model with citations and overlooked risks.

steps.title: Trace an important finding
steps.prompt: For [finding], show the exact document passages and page/section references supporting it. Walk through the inference step by step and separate disclosure from interpretation.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Explore a trial setback
steps.prompt: Model a narrow miss on the stated superiority endpoint. Explore whether an alternative trial or endpoint path is actually supported, then trace the conditional effects on timeline, cash runway, and valuation. Do not assume a regulatory option is available without evidence.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Stress-test the assumptions
steps.prompt: Rerun the scenario summary with a higher discount rate and lower probability of success using explicit input ranges. Show which scenario boundaries move most and where the middle case no longer holds.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Connect your career goals to a practical plan
summary: Compare target roles with your experience and separate future actions from proven achievements.
prerequisites: Provide your current resume and links to specific target roles.
Web research is needed for current opportunities; document and spreadsheet tools are needed for the deliverables.
outcome: A career action tracker and a skills portfolio workbook.

steps.title: Map the path
steps.prompt: Compare my resume with these target roles: [links]. Build an action tracker with prioritized skill gaps, portfolio projects, learning resources, people to contact, and milestones through [target date]. Separately create a skills portfolio workbook recording completed work, evidence, metrics, and competency-tagged interview stories. Do not invent achievements or treat planned work as completed.

steps.title: Prepare a conversation
steps.prompt: Research [company and role] before my conversation with [person]. Suggest informed questions about their work and identify relevant evidence from my portfolio. Update the action tracker with any new gaps this preparation reveals.

title: Consolidate project status across tools
summary: Reconcile messages, meetings, and documents into a task tracker with visible blockers.
prerequisites: Project name, reporting period, emails, channel history, documents, and meeting notes
Connected sources or exports; spreadsheet generation
outcome: A source-linked Excel tracker and an executive status brief.

steps.title: Build the task tracker
steps.prompt: Consolidate [project] updates from the last two weeks of email, its team channel, project documents, and meeting notes. For each task, record owner, current status, blockers, blocker age where supported, plans, and source context. Resolve conflicting updates by date and flag unresolved disagreements. Create an Excel tracker with status/priority dropdowns, source comments, and useful visual indicators; do not invent progress percentages.

steps.title: Trace a blocker
steps.prompt: Find every available mention of [blocker] across the sources. Reconstruct its escalation history, decisions, owner, and latest supported status, with timestamps and links.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Brief leadership
steps.prompt: Create a one-page report from the tracker with overall progress using an explicit defensible definition, blocker count, at-risk workstreams, and three items requiring leadership attention. State missing coverage.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Consolidate spreadsheet exports reliably
summary: Join source files into an updateable workbook without losing unmatched records.
prerequisites: Attach exports, confirm the joining key, metric definitions, targets, and refresh expectations.
outcome: A consolidated workbook with dashboard, reconciliation, and refresh instructions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Combine the supplied exports into one refreshable workbook using [confirmed record key]. Inspect duplicate and conflicting records before joining. Calculate [metrics], compare [actuals or pipeline] with [target], and build a clear dashboard with charts and explanatory notes. Preserve originals and include a review section for unmatched keys and conflicts. Document assumptions, refresh steps, and changes. Do not invent a join key or silently merge incompatible records.

steps.title: Test the refresh
steps.prompt: Refresh the workbook with [new export] and verify that overlapping records are not duplicated. Reconcile row counts and totals, report unmatched keys, and update the change log.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Convert a customer meeting into follow-ups
summary: Draft consistent customer, account, and internal updates from meeting evidence.
prerequisites: Provide the meeting transcript, summary, account context, and intended destinations.
outcome: A source-backed meeting recap and separate unsent follow-up drafts.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Use [customer meeting transcript and summary] to identify decisions, risks, opportunities, and explicit commitments with owners and dates. Name any missing source before drafting. Prepare a customer follow-up email, an account-plan update, CRM notes, and an internal team message. Ground important claims in the transcript and keep internal-only information out of the customer version. Flag uncertain ownership or timing instead of inventing commitments. Return the drafts separately; do not create records, assign work, send email, or post messages.

steps.title: Compare recurring calls
steps.prompt: Compare this call with the previous three. Highlight new decisions, changed commitments, emerging risks, and unresolved actions. Update the drafts only where the evidence changed and flag missing transcripts.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Coordinate a student team project
summary: Bring milestones, owners, budget, decisions, and communication into one plan.
prerequisites: Provide project notes, member availability, budget, campus rules, and deadlines.
outcome: A proposed project hub and reviewable operating materials.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Organize [club, event, or team project] using the shared notes, budget, member availability, campus requirements, and deadlines. Propose a clear folder structure, milestones, owner tracker, budget sheet, next-meeting agenda, communications drafts, and a decision/risk log. Link important requirements to their source and flag unresolved choices. Keep owner assignments and external communication as proposals until the team approves them; do not reorganize files or send messages without agreement.

title: Create a client-specific sales proposal deck
summary: Connect discovery evidence, the RFP, pricing, and relevant proof into a concise proposal.
prerequisites: Discovery notes, RFP, competitive analysis, approved pricing, and relevant case study
Brand logo and reference deck; presentation generation
outcome: A seven-slide editable deck with verified claims and clear next steps.

steps.title: Build the proposal
steps.prompt: Create an approximately seven-slide proposal for [client] using the supplied discovery notes, RFP, pricing sheet, and approved case study. Cover the executive summary, client challenges, tailored solution, implementation, pricing, proof, and timeline/next steps. Reuse the client's terminology and our brand references. Cite sensitive pricing and outcome claims in notes, and inspect the deck for clipping and overlap.

steps.title: Clarify the pricing slide
steps.prompt: Separate implementation charges from recurring subscription fees. Move support detail into a concise note and preserve clear assumptions, units, and the deck's visual consistency.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Lead with the client's priorities
steps.prompt: Rewrite the executive summary around the three challenges evidenced in discovery, followed by how our solution addresses them. Use the RFP's language and keep it to four focused bullets.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Create a coordinated classroom pack
summary: Keep teacher, student, and family materials consistent with the approved lesson.
prerequisites: Provide the reviewed lesson deck, unit plan, school guidance, and existing classroom materials.
outcome: A teacher guide, student handout, answer key, family overview, and materials list.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Create a classroom pack from the reviewed [lesson deck and unit plan]. Produce a teacher guide, student handout, answer key, one-page family overview, and materials checklist. Keep terminology, examples, timing, directions, and answers aligned across files. Follow the supplied school guidance and use only approved content. Check that each activity has the resources and instructions it needs. Flag accessibility, translation, or policy decisions that require review before use.

title: Create a custom security-review workflow
summary: Run repeatable reviews on chosen triggers and retain their evidence.
prerequisites: Provide the repository, current scanner documentation, approved runner, secret-store setup, and desired triggers.
outcome: A reviewable CI workflow that preserves reports and uses limited permissions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Draft a GitHub Actions security-review workflow for [repository] using the currently supported scanner integration. Support [manual or scheduled triggers], use an explicit reviewed revision, and keep checkout credentials and job permissions limited to what the scan needs. Reference secrets through the CI secret store. Preserve readable findings, machine-readable results, and coverage evidence, including failed runs. Explain any SARIF requirements and artifact-access implications. Validate the workflow structure and provide the controlled first-run procedure before enabling it.

title: Create a daily work briefing
summary: Bring commitments, decisions, messages, and blockers into one concise view.
prerequisites: Connect or provide the relevant calendar, messages, email, documents, and project trackers.
outcome: A source-linked briefing with the next decisions and actions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review my available work sources and prepare today's briefing. Establish my active projects, collaborators, commitments, and upcoming meetings. Prioritize changed deadlines, decisions I owe, unanswered messages, and work blocked on someone else. Check recent thread activity so resolved items do not resurface. Link every actionable item to its source, separate assumptions from confirmed facts, and name missing sources. Draft useful replies or meeting notes without sending or editing anything. Finish with the few actions that most need my attention today.

steps.title: Watch for meaningful changes
steps.prompt: Design an hourly check of the same approved sources. Notify me only when a decision, deadline, blocker, or message materially changes. Show the schedule and source access required; activate it only after approval and report if scheduling is unavailable.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Create a dedicated project briefing partner
summary: Maintain focused context on one workstream and its next decisions.
prerequisites: Provide the project scope and relevant messages, documents, calendar events, and tracker access.
outcome: A current project brief with source-linked decisions, blockers, and next steps.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Act as a briefing partner for [project] only. Review the relevant available documents, messages, meetings, and tracker to establish the goal, current state, people, decisions, deadlines, and open questions. Check later replies before resurfacing old requests and report inaccessible sources. Start with a concise brief: what changed, what is blocked, what decision is needed, and the next useful action. Support research, meeting preparation, and draft review as the project develops. Ask before sending, editing shared material, scheduling checks, or making commitments.

steps.title: Catch up on a change
steps.prompt: Update the project brief using [new sources or time window]. Highlight only material changes to decisions, deadlines, dependencies, and next actions, with links to the supporting evidence.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Create a fillable event-registration PDF
summary: Build a branded form with real interactive fields and a clear response structure.
prerequisites: Event details, ticket options and prices, required fields, and brand references
PDF generation supporting AcroForm fields; a PDF reader for functional testing
outcome: A tested fillable PDF and a consolidated registration workbook.

steps.title: Build the interactive form
steps.prompt: Create a fillable registration PDF for [event, dates, venue, contact]. Include required name/email fields; optional organization and job title; a ticket dropdown with the supplied prices; dietary checkboxes and details; session-interest checkboxes; and separate communication and sponsor-sharing choices. Use genuine PDF form fields with unique names and logical tab order. Match the brand and verify that entries can be saved and reopened.

steps.title: Apply the brand assets
steps.prompt: Update the form with the uploaded logo and exact style-guide colors while preserving field names, functionality, and the established layout.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Consolidate responses
steps.prompt: Extract completed form fields into an Excel workbook with one row per attendee. Flag missing required fields or duplicates and add a summary of ticket choices, dietary needs, and session interest.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Create a translated form
steps.prompt: Create a Spanish-language version with translated labels and option text. Preserve the field structure, ticket meanings, design, and ability to collect comparable responses.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Create a native Mac app workspace
summary: Build a SwiftUI shell with coordinated navigation, inspector, menus, and settings.
prerequisites: Requires a macOS development environment, Xcode, and an app brief or existing repository.
outcome: A working Mac app shell with native controls and reproducible build steps.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build a Mac-native SwiftUI shell for [app]. Use a main WindowGroup and a separate Settings scene. Coordinate a lightweight sidebar, detail view, and inspector with explicit selection state. Put primary actions in menus, toolbars, and keyboard shortcuts. Use window-scoped storage for navigation and app storage for preferences. Prefer semantic colors and native materials; introduce an AppKit bridge only for a specific behavior SwiftUI cannot express. Add a reusable build-and-run script, exercise the main navigation and preferences, and report the exact verification commands.

title: Create a paid-media performance recap
summary: Turn channel exports into a campaign review, a presentation, and a team digest.
prerequisites: Ad-platform exports, conversion data, campaign brief, and previous recap
Spreadsheet and presentation generation; connected Slack only if publishing is requested
outcome: A recap deck, refreshable analysis, and a concise Slack-ready summary.

steps.title: Build the recap
steps.prompt: Analyze the supplied paid-media data for [campaign and period]. Compare spend, reach, conversions, and pipeline contribution across channels. Explain what improved, what deteriorated, and what to change next. Create a concise recap deck, an analysis table that can be refreshed with the same inputs, and a Slack-ready digest of the three largest movers. Link conclusions to the supporting metrics.

steps.title: Capture the reporting method
steps.prompt: Write reusable reporting instructions with metric definitions, attribution assumptions, source locations, deck structure, and the three-mover digest format.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Set up the next recap
steps.prompt: Define a Monday 8 a.m. refresh in [timezone] using the same campaign sources. Specify where the analysis and deck belong and draft the message for #paid-media. Schedule or publish only through available connected tools; otherwise return the task and message for manual use.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Create a personalized first-week guide
summary: Bring a new hire's schedule, logistics, team, and access information into one welcome document.
prerequisites: New-hire details, start date, manager, company handbook, and office logistics
Calendar and team information through connected tools or supplied exports
outcome: A tailored onboarding guide with practical links and clear first-week actions.

steps.title: Build the welcome guide
steps.prompt: Create a first-week guide for [name, role, team, start date, manager]. Use the supplied handbook, logistics, calendar events, and team information to cover expectations, personal schedule, contacts, workplace details, tools/access, and common questions. Make it warm and easy to scan. Verify dates and timezone; mark any access or meeting that is not yet confirmed.

steps.title: Personalize a hiring cohort
steps.prompt: Create a separate guide for each person in [new-hire list]. Reuse company-wide facts while checking each person's role, manager, team, and actual schedule independently.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Add visual navigation
steps.prompt: Incorporate the supplied team photo and office map. Add useful links for addresses, contacts, policies, and tools, with readable captions and navigation.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Provide alternate formats
steps.prompt: Convert the approved guide into a printable PDF, a short email of urgent information and actions, and a concise onboarding presentation. Keep details consistent across formats.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Create a profile of your writing voice
summary: Learn your actual writing habits from sent messages and sharpen the profile through edits.
prerequisites: Provide writing samples or connect sent email, Slack, Microsoft 365, or Notion.
A persistent project or editable skill is needed to retain the profile across tasks.
outcome: A reusable voice guide with examples and explicit personal rules.

steps.title: Read my writing habits
steps.prompt: Study the attached writing samples or my recent sent messages. Describe my usual tone, sentence length, openings, requests, transitions, and sign-offs, with short examples. Separate consistent habits from choices that vary by audience. Turn this into a compact voice guide for drafting on my behalf.

steps.title: Learn from this edit
steps.prompt: Compare your draft with my edited version below. Identify the specific voice rules the edits reveal, add them to my profile, and retain the before-and-after example. Preserve rules I have explicitly set even if older samples conflict. Edited version: [paste].

title: Create a realistic day-by-day travel itinerary
summary: Combine personal interests, walking routes, current opening times, and practical alternatives.
prerequisites: Destination, dates, accommodation area, budget, interests, and mobility preferences
Current web research; calendar connection only for adding approved activities
outcome: A mobile-friendly travel document with timing, costs, locations, and fallback plans.

steps.title: Build the itinerary
steps.prompt: Plan a [five-day] trip to [destination and dates] around [interests], [walking preference], and [budget]. Research current opening hours and reservations, estimate realistic travel times, and group activities geographically. Create a mobile-readable Word document with daily timing, addresses, meal options, alternatives, approximate daily costs, and weather considerations. Link sources and image galleries; distinguish verified details from estimates.

steps.title: Improve the travel document
steps.prompt: Refine the document with a coherent color palette, readable typography, and tighter spacing while preserving useful detail and mobile legibility.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Add practical local context
steps.prompt: Research local etiquette, tipping, public transport, common visitor mistakes, and relevant customs. Use multiple current sources and distinguish local norms from optional preferences.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Add the approved schedule
steps.prompt: Add the approved activities to [calendar] with destination timezone, location, and useful notes. Check for conflicts and duplicates first. If calendar access is unavailable, return an importable calendar file instead.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Create a reusable visual-design refinement skill
summary: Codify a disciplined process for improving visual outputs before delivery.
prerequisites: Examples of preferred design and the kinds of outputs you create
A host supporting reusable skills for automatic activation; instructions can also be used manually
outcome: A design instruction package with checklists, techniques, references, and a tested refinement process.

steps.title: Build the design instruction package
steps.prompt: Create reusable instructions for refining presentations, dashboards, reports, spreadsheets, and HTML. Start from a functional version, then critique typography, color, hierarchy, spacing, and usability before revising. Include a delivery checklist, technique catalog, reference principles, refinement protocol, and a philosophy balancing distinctive choices with restraint. steps.title: Test the refinement process
