steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Trace how [request or feature] moves through this codebase, from entry point to response or persisted result. Explain which modules own each step, where inputs are validated, and where authentication, side effects, and error handling occur. Cite the actual files and symbols. Highlight important invariants and likely pitfalls for a developer changing this flow. Finish with the smallest useful set of files to read next. Keep observations separate from assumptions where runtime evidence is missing.

title: Map future cash pressure
summary: Build a formula-driven forecast that makes low-cash periods visible.
prerequisites: Attach cash balances, receipts, payment schedules, debt, tax, capex, and timing assumptions.
outcome: An editable cash forecast with liquidity thresholds and visible assumptions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build a cash forecast for [business and horizon] from the supplied files. Retain their weekly or monthly cadence. Model opening cash, collections, payroll, suppliers, debt, taxes, capital spending, and working-capital timing using formulas and explicit assumptions. Flag missing timing information instead of hiding a guessed value. Highlight the lowest closing balance, when it occurs, and any breach of [minimum cash threshold]. Deliver an editable workbook whose assumptions I can change without rebuilding the calculations.

steps.title: Stress-test collections
steps.prompt: Model [collection delay or payment change] without changing the base case. Compare the lowest cash balance and threshold breaches, and identify which timing assumptions explain the difference.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Map the arguments in your literature review
summary: See which papers reinforce, contradict, or bridge one another instead of grouping them only by topic.
prerequisites: Attach the papers or detailed notes, including claims and citations.
Interactive visualization tools are needed for an explorable map.
outcome: An argument map and a source-linked outline of the debate.

steps.title: Draw the debate
steps.prompt: Read these papers on [research topic]. Group them by the claims they defend, connect supporting arguments, and mark disagreements. Identify bridge papers and blind spots in each cluster. Cite the papers behind every connection and distinguish your interpretation from the authors' stated positions. Make an explorable argument map if visualization tools are available.

steps.title: Turn the map into a review
steps.prompt: Expand the disagreement between [cluster A] and [cluster B]: which claims conflict, which evidence each uses, and whether either side addresses the other. Then draft a state-of-the-debate outline organized by arguments and tensions, with citations and unresolved questions.

title: Map the prerequisites in your syllabus
summary: Identify which topic sequences are necessary and which weeks you can rearrange.
prerequisites: Attach a topic-by-week syllabus and specify the textbook or course-specific dependencies.
Interactive visualization support is needed for a clickable map.
outcome: A course dependency map and revised weekly schedule.

steps.title: Find the sequencing constraints
steps.prompt: Map the conceptual prerequisites in this [number]-week syllabus. For each topic, show what students need first and what it enables later. Distinguish firm dependencies from conventional ordering, label flexible sections, and explain alternative sequences. Include course-specific constraints I supplied instead of relying only on textbook order.

steps.title: Try a reorder
steps.prompt: Move [topic] to week [number] and show which later topics lose a prerequisite or need supporting material. Once we settle the order, write a revised weekly schedule with chapter mappings and explain the changes.

title: Migrate a legacy codebase in checkpoints
summary: Map compatibility risks before changing the stack.
prerequisites: Provide the current and target stacks, repository, public contracts, and build/test requirements.
outcome: An incremental migration with tested checkpoints and rollback options.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Plan the migration from [legacy stack] to [target stack] in this repository. Inventory routing, data models, authentication, configuration, build tooling, tests, deployment, and external contracts. Map each existing capability to its target equivalent and highlight gaps. Define small milestones with compatibility layers and rollback options where needed. Preserve behavior unless a change is explicitly required. At each implemented checkpoint, run the relevant type, lint, and focused tests and resolve failures before continuing. Start by presenting the migration map and checkpoint plan.

title: Migrate a validation module without contract drift
summary: Compare the same public contract before and after a bounded dependency change.
prerequisites: Provide the module, pinned baseline/target versions, migration guide, callers, frozen contract tests, and isolated environment.
outcome: A scoped migration with before-and-after contract evidence and rollback notes.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Migrate [validation module] from [pinned baseline] to [approved target] within [scope]. Record the starting revision, runtime and dependency versions, and lockfile hash. Read the official guide, callers, public contracts, and repository instructions; run the baseline first. Keep broader dependency preparation separate. Run the same frozen HTTP contract tests through the real router and serialization before and after the change, comparing statuses, headers, accepted inputs, defaults, nulls, JSON shapes, and full errors. Do not weaken assertions or approve new snapshots to hide differences. Return the diff, exact validation evidence, unresolved incompatibilities, and rollback plan without merging or deploying.

title: Modernize an AI API integration
summary: Upgrade the supported API path while preserving application behavior.
prerequisites: Provide the repository, provider, current integration, target requirements, and access to official documentation.
outcome: A bounded migration with updated prompts, tests, and compatibility notes.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Inspect this [AI provider] integration and inventory models, endpoints, tool contracts, response handling, and prompt assumptions. Consult current official documentation for the supported migration path and model-specific prompting guidance. Propose the smallest upgrade that meets [requirements], then implement it within the approved scope. Preserve observable behavior unless the new API requires a change. Test tool calls and response shapes, and explicitly flag manual review points or unsupported features. Do not assume a model-name substitution is a complete migration.

title: Onboard a batch of vendors
summary: Coordinate vendor details, contract templates, a tracker, and procurement intake forms in one workflow.
prerequisites: Requires local file access, document and spreadsheet editing, and browser control signed into the procurement portal.
Provide vendor records, approved NDA and MSA templates, and the current tracker.
outcome: Per-vendor document folders, updated tracker rows, and forms ready for review.

steps.title: Process the vendor batch
steps.prompt: For each vendor in [folder], reconcile contact and commercial details, fill our NDA and MSA templates, and complete the procurement intake form for review. Add the verified fields and current onboarding status to the tracker. Save each vendor's documents together and record missing information instead of guessing or duplicating an existing vendor.

steps.title: Check the batch
steps.prompt: Cross-check every generated agreement, portal form, and tracker row against its source vendor record. List discrepancies and incomplete fields, correct supported errors, and give me a per-vendor completion checklist before forms are submitted.

title: Optimize next quarter's campaign budget
summary: Compare campaign and channel results, then model practical budget shifts.
prerequisites: Campaign-level impressions, clicks, conversions, spend, and segment data
ROI target, lifetime-value assumptions, benchmarks, and budget-shift limit
outcome: A performance dashboard and a justified budget-reallocation recommendation.

steps.title: Analyze performance and reallocate
steps.prompt: Analyze [quarter] campaign data across social, search, and email. Rank campaigns and channels by ROI, acquisition cost, and conversion rate. Compare customer segments using [lifetime-value assumptions]. Recommend the next quarter's allocation within [maximum shift], show the calculations, and distinguish projections from observed results. Deliver an Excel dashboard and a written action plan using [ROI target and benchmark].

steps.title: Standardize earlier reports
steps.prompt: Reformat the attached historical performance reviews into this reporting structure. Preserve their original numbers and findings; flag any metrics that cannot be compared consistently.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Improve exploration
steps.prompt: Add useful trend charts, performance heat maps, and filters to the workbook. Keep metric formulas visible and verify that the visuals reconcile to the source totals.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Organize a job search with verified evidence
summary: Compare roles and tailor application drafts without inventing qualifications.
prerequisites: Provide job descriptions, resume, verified experience, portfolio, contacts, and application deadlines.
outcome: A role-by-role application tracker and reviewable tailored materials.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Compare these [job or internship] opportunities against my resume, verified experience, portfolio, and career guidance. Build one tracker row per role with requirements, evidence of fit, gaps, current status, deadline, and next action. Organize the supporting material by role and draft tailored application content that uses only claims I can support. Mark missing evidence clearly. Do not submit applications, contact people, or send documents without my approval.

title: Organize a lesson folder
summary: Make teaching files easier to find without losing original versions.
prerequisites: Provide the lesson folder, naming preferences, and permission to inspect its contents.
outcome: A proposed folder structure, version inventory, and verified change record.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Inspect [lesson or unit folder] and propose a clear organization. Identify duplicate files, older drafts, unclear names, and the current approved materials. Suggest subfolders, consistent names, an archive for superseded drafts, and a short README explaining the contents. Keep original source files intact. Show the proposed moves and renames before applying them; after approval, verify the resulting folder and list every change.

title: Organize a semester workspace
summary: Connect course materials and assignments to a verified deadline tracker.
prerequisites: Provide syllabi, assignment sheets, semester files, and course naming conventions.
outcome: A course-indexed workspace plan and a source-linked deadline tracker.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Organize the supplied semester materials by course, separating official documents, readings, notes, assignments, and submitted work. Inventory duplicates and versions, propose consistent file names, and create a course index. Extract deadlines from official syllabi and assignment sheets, link each date to its source, and flag conflicts or missing time zones instead of guessing. Preserve originals and show the planned archive, move, and rename operations before changing files.

title: Organize a volunteer program
summary: Build consistent role, onboarding, communication, and tracking materials for a growing program.
prerequisites: Organization mission, volunteer roles, program scale, training and background-check policies
Existing handbook, brand references, and tracking requirements
outcome: A connected volunteer operations toolkit ready for staff review.

steps.title: Build the operating toolkit
steps.prompt: Using the supplied program information, create role descriptions for tutors, reading-group volunteers, event coordinators, and administrative support. Produce a welcome packet, onboarding checklist, training timeline, background-check procedure, and handbook reflecting our actual policies. Add welcome/reminder/recognition/check-in templates and a workbook tracking contacts, roles, hours, certifications, training, and students served. Use a warm, practical tone and mark policy decisions still needed.

steps.title: Add specialist roles
steps.prompt: Add curriculum-developer and family-engagement-coordinator role descriptions using the same structure. Define responsibilities, training, time commitment, and supervision based on the program context.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Evaluate the program
steps.prompt: Create a quarterly satisfaction survey, annual impact assessment, retention tracker, and improvement-plan template. Define the measures and provide practical questions and analysis guidance.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare recruitment materials
steps.prompt: Create a one-page overview, social posts emphasizing different benefits, an interest form, and presentation talking points. Use supported impact figures and concrete expectations for prospective volunteers.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Organize clinician-reviewed exercise notes
summary: Research and format an exercise discussion guide that is easy to review on a phone.
prerequisites: Clinician's recommendations, exercise restrictions, and relevant symptoms
Current reputable medical sources; Apple Notes connection only for direct saving
outcome: A concise routine draft and progress tracker for review with a clinician.

steps.title: Prepare the review notes
steps.prompt: My clinician recommended strengthening the muscles around my knee. Using [their instructions and restrictions], research suitable exercise options from reputable medical sources and prepare a concise mobile-readable note for my physical therapist to review. Include technique cues, questions to ask, and symptoms that should stop an exercise. Do not diagnose my knee condition. Save to [notes app] if connected, or provide copyable text.

steps.title: Track the agreed routine
steps.prompt: Create an Excel tracker for the clinician-approved routine with date, exercise, sets/reps, pain before and after, modifications, and notes. Add weekly totals and trends without treating improvement as proof of a diagnosis.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Understand the anatomy
steps.prompt: Explain the anatomy of [clinician-confirmed condition] and how the prescribed exercises relate to it. Separate established information from uncertain mechanisms and link reputable sources.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Discuss progression
steps.prompt: Based on the progress log, outline questions and possible progression options to discuss with my physical therapist. Keep them within the stated restrictions and do not assume a harder routine is appropriate solely because it feels easier.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Organize evidence for a compliance audit
summary: Turn scattered documents into a control-based inventory and expose missing evidence.
prerequisites: Requires a desktop agent with access to the audit folder and document-reading tools.
Provide the control framework, audit scope, and review period; ticket-system evidence requires its connector or browser access.
outcome: A renamed evidence collection, coverage matrix, and audit walkthrough notes.

steps.title: Inventory and map evidence
steps.prompt: Review all files in [audit folder] against [framework], covering [scope] for [period]. Propose descriptive names including document type, effective date, and control area, and group documents by control. Produce an old-to-new name map and flag uncertain classifications, out-of-period evidence, and apparent coverage gaps before reorganizing.

steps.title: Create the control matrix
steps.prompt: Build a spreadsheet with control ID, requirement, supporting documents, covered dates, and evidence status. Separate absent evidence from a demonstrated control failure. Add a one-page policy reference for the walkthrough and list records we should obtain from [ticket system].

title: Organize files by what they contain
summary: Sort a cluttered folder using the substance of the files and keep a clear record of every move.
prerequisites: Requires a desktop agent with permission to read and move files in the selected folder.
Specify excluded files, active project folders, naming preferences, and permitted cleanup rules.
outcome: A navigable folder structure and a searchable old-to-new location map.

steps.title: Sort the folder
steps.prompt: Inspect the files in [folder] and group them by their contents and practical use. Keep [excluded items] untouched. Propose a small folder structure, then organize the files within the granted access. Preserve a mapping of old and new paths, flag ambiguous items, and do not delete files unless they match my stated cleanup rules.

steps.title: Make the system maintainable
steps.prompt: Refine the folders using [client, project, language, or date] as the organizing rule. Tell me where [file description] moved, and write simple filing rules for future downloads so I can maintain this structure.

title: Package a repeatable workflow as a skill
summary: Capture a proven process with reusable instructions, commands, and output expectations.
prerequisites: Provide a successful example, supporting runbook or thread, reusable commands, and the target agent platform.
outcome: A reusable skill grounded in a demonstrated workflow.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Create a reusable agent skill for [recurring task]. Learn from [successful example] and [runbook, review, or discussion]. Identify the inputs, sequence, decision points, reusable scripts, validation commands, and expected output. Preserve the important behavior from the working example while removing one-off details. Make instructions specific enough for another run to follow and clearly state when the skill applies. Verify its format against the target platform and test it with a representative task rather than inventing untested capabilities.

title: Plan a behavior-preserving refactor
summary: Break structural cleanup into small passes with explicit parity checks.
prerequisites: Provide the repository, refactor goals, supported public contracts, and validation commands.
outcome: A staged refactor plan that separates cleanup from migrations and behavior changes.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Inspect this codebase for dead code, duplicated logic, oversized modules, stale abstractions, and legacy patterns that make changes difficult. Propose small reviewable refactor passes. For each, describe the existing behavior, the structural improvement, and the check that will establish parity. Preserve public APIs and user-visible behavior. Separate framework migrations, dependency upgrades, and architecture changes into their own decisions. For broad work, identify the specifications and compatibility checks needed before implementation. Return the plan first.

title: Plan a defensive AI access rollout
summary: Prepare a controlled access plan and verify that approved users can use the required security capability.
prerequisites: Provide the security-access program, current official setup guide, workspace state, and approved member list.
outcome: An owner-reviewed rollout checklist with access verification and unresolved requirements.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prepare an access-rollout checklist for [approved defensive security program] in [workspace]. Use the current official instructions and the workspace evidence I provide. Separate pending application or verification from active access. Identify the authorized owner, approved members, required model permissions, role or group assignments, and how to check for unintended access through other roles. Treat API-project access as a separate setup when applicable. Propose a small benign verification task for an approved user and document troubleshooting checks. Do not submit attestations, change roles, or grant access; return the concrete steps for owner review.

title: Plan thoughtful gifts you can actually find
summary: Use details about each person to move from generic ideas to a practical shopping list.
prerequisites: Provide recipients' interests, useful preferences, budget, location, and shopping deadline.
Current web search is required for products and availability; personal notes or messages are optional evidence.
outcome: A recipient-based shortlist and an efficient store-by-store plan.

steps.title: Build a personal shortlist
steps.prompt: Suggest gifts for these people: [details]. Stay within [budget] and prioritize things that fit a real interest, improve a routine, or solve a small annoyance. Ask targeted questions where the context is thin. Research specific options available near [location] by [date], cite current prices and stock evidence, and explain why each gift fits.

steps.title: Plan the shopping run
steps.prompt: Use the chosen shortlist to group purchases by store and minimize travel. Include online backups where local availability is uncertain. Search these supplied notes or connected messages for specific hints I may have forgotten, keeping them separate from your inferred suggestions.

title: Plan time and money together
summary: See workload conflicts and upcoming payments in a practical weekly view.
prerequisites: Provide course and work calendars, recurring commitments, income, bills, and expense categories.
outcome: A personal planning dashboard with adjustable assumptions and next-week options.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build a planning view from my course calendar, work shifts, recurring commitments, income, bills, and expense categories. Show weekly scheduling conflicts, heavy workload periods, upcoming payment dates, and an adjustable budget. Suggest practical options for [next week] and explain their time and cost tradeoffs. Keep unknown income or expenses marked as missing rather than estimating them silently. Do not change events, send messages, or make financial transactions.

title: Plan your week from calendar and inbox evidence
summary: See the real workload behind your meetings, unresolved messages, and preparation commitments.
prerequisites: Connect Microsoft 365 for Outlook calendar and email, plus accessible SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams context.
Specify the week, working hours, timezone, and priorities.
outcome: A practical weekly plan with email priorities and protected focus time.

steps.title: Build the weekly plan
steps.prompt: Plan [dates] from my calendar and inbox. Identify meetings requiring preparation or decisions, overlapping commitments, and usable focus blocks after accounting for prep. Find weekend messages, older threads becoming urgent, and people blocked by my response. Produce a compact daily plan with must-dos, suggested deep-work time, and email triage, citing the relevant items.

steps.title: Prepare the highest-stakes meeting
steps.prompt: For [meeting], collect the related correspondence and documents. Write a one-page brief with expected decisions, advance questions, required figures, and missing inputs. Draft replies for the urgent threads we identified, leaving them for me to review.

title: Post a weekly team status from actual work
summary: Combine team conversation and tracker state into a digest people can correct before forwarding.
prerequisites: Requires a channel assistant with scheduled routines and access to Linear or Jira.
GitHub is optional for merged pull requests; define channels, tracker scope, schedule, and timezone.
outcome: A recurring channel update with decisions, open work, and blocked owners.

steps.title: Schedule the team digest
steps.prompt: Every [weekday, time, timezone], post a draft weekly update in [team channel] using this channel's discussions and the connected tracker. Cover decisions made, work completed, items still open, and dependencies waiting on named owners. Link evidence, check current ticket state, and distinguish shipped work from tickets merely marked complete.

steps.title: Expand and correct the digest
steps.prompt: Include [additional channel], [repository], and [launch tracker] in the next run. Show how long each blocked item has been stuck against plan and its owner. Apply these corrections: [details], then list the configured schedule and sources so the team can verify the routine.

title: Practice a case interview with rigorous feedback
summary: Use a model to explore a business case, then test the numbers and logic in your recommendation.
prerequisites: Upload the practice case and any supporting exhibits.
Requires spreadsheet creation for formula-driven models and scenario inputs.
outcome: A case-analysis workbook, practice questions, and specific coaching.

steps.title: Set up the practice
steps.prompt: Extract the facts and numbers from this case into a spreadsheet with clearly labeled source data, formulas, and adjustable assumptions. Provide the relevant analytical framework and questions I should investigate, but let me form my own recommendation. Distinguish missing inputs from values supported by the case.

steps.title: Review my recommendation
steps.prompt: Here is my analysis: [paste]. Check the calculations, reasoning chain, untested assumptions, and practicality. Give specific improvements as an experienced case interviewer, then show one equally defensible alternative analytical route and what it would emphasize.

title: Practice a debate against strong opposition
summary: Pressure-test a position with substantive counterarguments and focused feedback.
prerequisites: Debate topic, position, format, and evidence to use
A live AI integration is required for a standalone adaptive app; conversational practice works directly in chat
outcome: A practice dialogue, weakness analysis, and concise response cards.

steps.title: Start the debate practice
steps.prompt: Help me practice defending [position] on [topic]. Present the strongest reasonable opposing case, ask one challenging question at a time, and adapt to my answers. Use real evidence where available and label uncertainty. If building a standalone simulator, create a restrained paper-like interface and explicitly identify the AI integration needed for live responses rather than presenting scripted replies as adaptive intelligence.

steps.title: Analyze my weak points
steps.prompt: Review my responses. For each weakness, explain the flawed assumption or missing evidence, how an opponent could challenge it, and a stronger response that does not overclaim.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Create response cards
steps.prompt: Identify five likely questions and draft conversational 30-second answers that address each directly with appropriate evidence. Keep them concise enough to rehearse naturally.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Practice a difficult rhetorical turn
steps.prompt: Simulate an opponent responding to my evidence with an emotionally compelling anecdote. Coach me to acknowledge the human concern while returning respectfully to the question and relevant evidence.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Prepare a committee decision packet
summary: Bring governance evidence, options, and meeting structure into one reviewable package.
prerequisites: Provide prior minutes, policies, stakeholder feedback, data, governance rules, and the meeting deadline.
outcome: A sourced committee packet with options, agenda, and draft minutes template.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prepare the packet for [committee and decision]. Use the supplied minutes, policy drafts, stakeholder views, program data, governance requirements, and evaluation criteria. State the question to resolve, organize the evidence, compare options and tradeoffs, and surface unresolved issues. Propose a focused agenda and a minutes template that captures decisions and follow-ups. Distinguish findings from recommendations and leave the final judgment to the committee.

title: Prepare a daily cross-tool briefing
summary: Connect dashboard alerts, conversations, and tasks into one morning view.
prerequisites: Slack and Notion access or exported messages and tasks
Access to the team dashboard; browser capability if it is not available through a connector
outcome: A prioritized briefing with context, blockers, and linked evidence.

steps.title: Build the morning briefing
steps.prompt: Prepare my morning briefing from [Slack channels], [Notion workspace], and [team dashboard URL]. Lead with urgent or deteriorating dashboard signals, then full threads mentioning me, relevant discussions I am missing, and tasks due this week with blockers. For urgent items, explain the people involved, prior discussion, and unresolved decision. Link evidence and identify any inaccessible source.

steps.title: Investigate an alert
steps.prompt: Investigate [dashboard alert] using its related conversations and tasks. Explain the timeline, contributing factors, owners, and the next unresolved action.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Draft a contextual reply
steps.prompt: Draft a reply to [thread] using the full context. Confirm the intended next step while clearly flagging [dependency]. Keep the message ready for my review.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Connect one topic across tools
steps.prompt: Find what has been discussed about [topic] across messages, task records, and dashboard information. Reconcile decisions, dates, and open questions into one brief.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Prepare a deal using comparable opportunities
summary: Learn from similar wins and losses before your next buyer conversation.
prerequisites: Connect Salesforce or HubSpot and provide the current buyer profile, deal size, and concerns.
Web research is needed only for current competitor positioning.
outcome: A concise deal brief with comparables, objections, and practical talking points.

steps.title: Find comparable deals
steps.prompt: For this opportunity: [industry, company size, value, product, concerns], find comparable wins and losses from the past [period]. Compare sales-cycle length, final terms, objections, implementation needs, and stage progression. Cite CRM records, identify colleagues with relevant experience, and make a scan-friendly brief that explains both the similarities and the limits of the comparison.

steps.title: Prepare the conversation
steps.prompt: Investigate the closest comparable deal in more detail, then draft five conversational talking points for this buyer's concerns. Ground each in the record and distinguish observed outcomes from promises we cannot make.

title: Prepare a new-hire onboarding packet
summary: Stage readiness trackers and welcome materials using approved hiring information.
prerequisites: Provide the approved new-hire roster, start-date window, manager mapping, tracker template, and announcement/privacy rules.
outcome: A staged tracker update, readiness-gap list, and private welcome plan.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prepare onboarding drafts for accepted hires starting during [date range]. Use only [approved roster and mapping sources]. Check source fields and group hires by team and manager; flag missing role, start date, work contact, buddy, location, or equipment/account readiness. Propose tracker updates and a team summary. Draft welcome-space names, membership, and messages only within the approved announcement and privacy rules. Exclude compensation, identity documents, medical details, interview notes, and other unrelated sensitive information. Return the staged rows and exact drafts for review without changing HR records, inviting people, creating channels, or sending messages.

steps.title: Review readiness gaps
steps.prompt: Prioritize the missing onboarding information by what blocks the start date. For each gap, identify the appropriate owner from the approved mapping and draft a minimal clarification request without exposing the full roster.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Prepare a sprint retrospective and operations handoff
summary: Combine ticket movement with team discussion to explain delivery and prepare the next rotation.
prerequisites: Connect Linear and Slack; PagerDuty is optional for complete paging data.
Provide the closed cycle, channel window, retro template, previous retro, and outstanding action list.
outcome: A focused retrospective and a separate operational handoff.

steps.title: Draft both documents
steps.prompt: Read [closed cycle] and [date range] in the team and on-call channels. Draft a retrospective covering completed work, slipped work with supported reasons, and a few themes worth discussing. Separately write the operational handoff covering open alerts, repeated toil, and watch items. Link evidence and keep the retrospective realistic for a 30-minute meeting.

steps.title: Carry actions forward
steps.prompt: Check last sprint's commitments against this cycle's evidence. Identify actions completed, still open, or ineffective, and propose a short discussion agenda with concrete decisions the team needs to make. Add unresolved operational items to the handoff.

title: Prepare a vendor renewal negotiation
summary: Compare contract changes and ground your negotiation position in usage, spend, and alternatives.
prerequisites: Provide the signed agreement, renewal proposal, usage export, comparable quotes, and approved fallback positions.
Drive and Brex can supply contract and spend records; Slack can supply stakeholder needs.
outcome: A clause comparison and a one-page negotiation brief.

steps.title: Build the negotiation brief
steps.prompt: Compare the current agreement and renewal proposal for [vendor]. Create a table of material changes with clause reference, current term, proposed term, and our policy-based position. Use actual spend, usage, and comparable offers to identify leverage. Draft a one-page brief with likely pushback, three asks ranked by value, and the walk-away conditions we have actually authorized.

steps.title: Prepare the tradeoffs
steps.prompt: For each priority ask, show an opening position, acceptable fallback, and what we could trade in return. Distinguish evidence-backed leverage from assumptions and list decisions procurement or legal must settle before the call.

title: Prepare a web app preview deployment
summary: Build the requested site and verify a reviewable deployment.
prerequisites: Provide source code or a brief, required assets, and an authorized deployment account.
outcome: A verified preview URL with build results and remaining limitations.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Build or update [website] using [repository, screenshots, or brief]. Follow [product and style constraints] and preserve [unchanged areas]. Complete the required interactions, run the local build, and inspect the result. Using the approved hosting connection, deploy a preview and verify that the deployment is ready before returning its URL. If hosting access is unavailable, return the working local version and exact missing setup rather than claiming a deployment succeeded.

title: Prepare an evidence-based meeting brief
summary: Arrive with the objective, context, agenda, and decisions clearly organized.
prerequisites: Provide the meeting date, calendar event, and specific notes, documents, or threads to consult.
outcome: A concise meeting brief with sources, questions, and a notes template.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prepare me for [meeting] on [date]. Use only [named calendar event, documents, notes, and discussion threads]. Start by confirming accessible sources and identifying gaps. Explain the meeting objective, relevant attendee context, facts we should share, likely agenda, unresolved questions, and decisions or commitments I may owe. Link to supporting evidence. Add a practical notes template for decisions and follow-ups. Put unsupported assumptions in a separate section. Do not send messages, edit shared notes, or distribute the brief.

steps.title: Shorten the pre-read
steps.prompt: Condense this into a one-page pre-read with the objective, three essential facts, decisions needed, and the most consequential open questions. Retain source links.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Prepare an on-call rotation handoff
summary: Bring alerts, customer escalations, and recent deploys into one actionable shift brief.
prerequisites: Connect PagerDuty and Slack; connect GitHub or provide production deploy history.
Provide the handoff template, previous brief, runbook index, shift dates, and output destination.
Posting needs write access to the handoff channel.
outcome: A handoff with incident status, watch items, and runbook links.

steps.title: Write the handoff
steps.prompt: Review pages, incident threads, customer-support escalations, and production changes from [shift start] to [shift end]. For every relevant item, state whether it is resolved, under monitoring, or still open, its known cause, and what the next engineer must watch. Carry forward unresolved items from the last handoff, link runbooks, save the brief to [folder], and post it in [handoff channel].

steps.title: Reduce repeat alerts
steps.prompt: List alerts that fired more than three times this rotation. Separate actionable incidents from noise, identify any safe tuning proposals supported by the evidence, and add owners and follow-up links to the handoff.

title: Prepare an outside-counsel spend review
summary: Locate billing exceptions and explain the matters drifting beyond budget before the partner discussion.
prerequisites: Provide outside-counsel billing guidelines and matter budgets.
Connect iManage or NetDocuments for matter and invoice detail, and Microsoft 365 for Excel and Word outputs, or supply equivalent exports.
outcome: A matter-level variance table and evidence-linked partner talking points.

steps.title: Review the firm
steps.prompt: For [law firm and period], compare billing entries with our guidelines and actual matter spend with approved budgets. Flag specific off-policy entries, quantify each budget variance, and identify the activities driving it. Cite the underlying invoice or matter record, distinguish verified issues from questions, and draft concise talking points for the relationship partner.

steps.title: Build the discussion agenda
steps.prompt: Prioritize the largest or recurring exceptions. Create a negotiation agenda with the supporting amounts, questions for the firm, and proposed corrective actions. Include an Excel variance table and a Word briefing in our existing review format.

title: Prepare and verify a security patch
summary: Move a reviewed finding through a focused patch and evidence-based verification.
prerequisites: Provide the reviewed finding, affected repository, reproduction evidence, and supported test commands.
outcome: A focused patch, before-and-after evidence, and a draft review description.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Address [reviewed finding] in this repository. Confirm the vulnerable behavior and the legitimate behavior that must remain. Prepare the smallest focused patch with a regression test or repeatable validation artifact. Show the proposed diff before applying it when the review workflow supports that separation. Verify that the original issue no longer occurs and normal behavior still works; record exact commands and limitations. Prepare a review description linking the finding, code changes, and evidence. Do not close the finding, merge, or deploy solely because a patch was generated.

title: Prepare context and agendas for next week's calls
summary: Gather previous discussion and open commitments into one readable meeting-prep document.
prerequisites: Connect Google Calendar, Slack, and Gmail; Drive is optional for documents.
Provide agenda preferences, exclusions, and the planning folder; recurring delivery requires a scheduler.
outcome: A week-ahead briefing with a short agenda for every meeting and three prep priorities.

steps.title: Prepare the meeting week
steps.prompt: Review my calendar for [week]. For each meeting, find the last relevant discussion, related messages, referenced documents, and commitments I owe. Draft one compact agenda paragraph and link the source context. Flag the three meetings that need the most preparation and explain why, then save one combined week-ahead document.

steps.title: Create a weekly routine
steps.prompt: Schedule this briefing for [weekday, time, timezone], covering the following week. Save the combined brief and individual agendas in a dated folder under [Planning], carry forward unresolved prep items, and state which sources were unavailable on each run.

title: Prepare CRM activity logs from your calendar
summary: Match external meetings to contacts and draft consistent call records for review.
prerequisites: External calendar meetings, call summaries, and access to Salesforce records
Calendar/CRM connector or authenticated browser; CRM write access only for approved saves
outcome: Reviewed activity drafts with next steps and accurate CRM associations.

steps.title: Draft today's call logs
steps.prompt: Review today's calendar in [timezone] and select external meetings, excluding internal events and cancellations. Match attendees to Salesforce contacts and accounts, flag ambiguous matches, and ask me for a brief call summary where missing. Draft an activity record with discussion points and next steps for each meeting. Check for existing logs and show all drafts for review before saving anything.

steps.title: Update a reviewed opportunity
steps.prompt: For [confirmed opportunity], prepare these changes: stage [stage], close date [exact date], and competitor [name]. Show the current and proposed values, then apply only the changes I have approved.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Catch up on the week
steps.prompt: Repeat the draft-and-review process for external meetings in [date range]. Avoid duplicating activities already logged and group remaining drafts by account and meeting date.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Create a confirmed missing contact
steps.prompt: Create a contact for [confirmed person and account] using the supplied title and verified contact details from the meeting invitation or signature. Leave unknown fields blank. Then associate the approved activity with that record and report the saved result.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Prepare for a sales call
summary: Combine deal history, recent calls, and the action plan into focused meeting preparation.
prerequisites: CRM record, last three call transcripts, and mutual action plan
Calendar access for a daily batch; Salesforce and Drive access or exports
outcome: A call-prep sheet with priorities, asks, objections, and responses.

steps.title: Prepare the call sheet
steps.prompt: Prepare for my meeting with [account] on [date]. Use the CRM record, latest three call transcripts, and mutual action plan to explain deal status and buyer priorities. Recommend two or three specific asks for this call and likely objections with grounded responses. Highlight unresolved commitments and any conflicting information.

steps.title: Make preparation consistent
steps.prompt: Capture our discovery framework, objection-handling principles, and call-sheet format as reusable instructions. Apply my feedback to the examples.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the day's meetings
steps.prompt: Use today's external meetings to create one prep sheet per account with the same method. Prepare a weekday 7:30 a.m. routine in [timezone]; ongoing execution requires calendar, account-source, and scheduling access.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

summary: Cross-reference your calendar and email to surface preparation needs and missing rooms or links.

Calendar write access is needed for room bookings or video-link updates.
outcome: A daily prep list and a specific list of calendar fixes.

steps.title: Review tomorrow
steps.prompt: Read tomorrow's calendar and relevant correspondence. Classify meetings as internal or external using attendees' domains, link recent topic-related threads, and highlight materials worth reading. Check each in-person event for a suitable room and each remote event for a video link. Present the preparation list and proposed logistics fixes.

steps.title: Apply the chosen fixes
steps.prompt: For these approved events: [list], book an available room matching [location and capacity], and add or correct the video link where needed. Recheck availability before each booking and report exactly which calendar events changed.

title: Prepare vendor-contract redlines and negotiation points
summary: Focus a services agreement on exit flexibility, data ownership, and commercial constraints.

A document tool capable of genuine tracked changes and comments
outcome: A tracked-changes draft, prioritized comparison, and collaborative negotiation email.

steps.title: Create a reviewable redline
steps.prompt: Review the attached vendor-services agreement for [company context]. Focus on lock-in, termination and adjustment rights, ownership of our data and paid deliverables, and budget exposure. Preserve the original contract in a new copy and propose changes with genuine tracked changes and explanatory comments where the document tool supports them. Otherwise provide a clearly labeled clause-change table, not a simulated tracked-changes file.

steps.title: Draft the negotiation email
steps.prompt: Draft a collaborative email prioritizing the proposed edits. Explain the business reason for each essential change and offer compromise language where our stated position allows flexibility.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Show negotiation tradeoffs

steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Preserve family recipes as interactive cards
summary: Turn handwritten recipes into clear digital instructions while keeping the original keepsake.

Interactive HTML support; notes/reminder access only for saving directly
outcome: A shareable recipe card with serving adjustment and a consistent family collection.

steps.title: Create the recipe card
steps.prompt: Read the attached handwritten recipe and produce a clear ingredient list and cooking sequence. Flag uncertain handwriting and vague quantities; propose labeled estimates rather than presenting guesses as the original. Build a shareable interactive card with a serving-size adjuster, the original image, and a compact cultural-context section with verifiable sources. Do not imply live fact retrieval unless the app has a configured connection.

steps.title: Explain the cooking technique
steps.prompt: Walk through the recipe's key techniques, including ingredient order, browning, and the purpose of its base. Tie each explanation to this recipe rather than changing the family method without saying so.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the shopping trip
steps.prompt: Create a shopping list grouped by store section for [servings]. Save it to my notes and create a grocery reminder for [time] only if those apps are connected; otherwise provide the list and reminder text.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Build the family collection
steps.prompt: Format the additional uploaded recipes using the same layout, type, and colors. Create a table of contents and preserve the original photographs and uncertainty notes for each recipe.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Pressure-test a sales forecast
summary: Separate reliable commitments from upside and deals that need to move out.
prerequisites: Provide opportunity exports, forecast snapshots, calls, legal or procurement status, and owner notes.
outcome: A deal-by-deal forecast recommendation with evidence and follow-up questions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review [deals] for the [period] forecast. Reconcile current opportunity records with recent calls, messages, usage signals, support issues, and legal or procurement progress. Recommend which deals belong in commit, upside, or outside this period. Explain each recommendation using sourced facts and clearly labeled inference. Identify blockers, stale assumptions, missing evidence, and owner follow-ups for the forecast call. Keep the CRM and official forecast unchanged.

steps.title: Prepare the forecast discussion
steps.prompt: Turn the highest-risk recommendations into a short call agenda. For each deal, state the decision needed, the evidence to confirm, and the question its owner should answer.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Prioritize incoming bug reports
summary: Combine scattered reports into one evidence-based engineering queue.
prerequisites: Provide the repository or service, time window, and approved issue, alert, log, or support sources.
outcome: A deduplicated P0-P3 bug queue with evidence and next actions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Triage reports for [service or team] from [time window]. Read [approved issue queues, error monitoring, support tickets, and discussion threads]. State which sources are inaccessible. Consolidate reports of the same underlying problem, then rank bugs from P0 to P3. Give each a concise title, observed evidence with links, impact, and the next diagnostic or remediation action. Distinguish a demonstrated failure from an untested hypothesis. If nothing qualifies, say so. Keep the review read-only: do not create tickets, change assignments, rerun jobs, post messages, or start fixes.

steps.title: Repeat the triage
steps.prompt: Draft recurring triage instructions using these sources, priority definitions, and duplicate rules. Include the proposed schedule and how to handle missing sources or an empty result. Keep the run read-only and show the configuration before scheduling it.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Prioritize voice-of-customer themes for roadmap review
summary: Connect recurring feedback to severity, source evidence, and existing roadmap work.

Slack, Zendesk, and Linear access or exports
outcome: A one-page customer-voice brief with quantified themes and roadmap links.

steps.title: Create the customer-voice brief
steps.prompt: Read the supplied feedback folder, product-feedback discussions, and support tickets tagged feedback. Group the evidence into five to seven themes. Count occurrences without double-counting repeated reports, assess severity, and include representative quotes with source links. Identify which themes map to existing roadmap items and which are new. Write a one-page brief for roadmap review and flag sample limitations.

steps.title: Standardize the synthesis
steps.prompt: Capture the source list, deduplication method, severity criteria, roadmap-matching rules, and brief format as reusable instructions.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the weekly refresh
steps.prompt: Define a Friday 4 p.m. refresh of the current quarter's feedback sources, saving a dated brief and highlighting changes since last review. A recurring run requires access to the feedback systems and scheduling support.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

summary: Turn a flow specification and component library into a browser-testable prototype.

Figma and GitHub access or local exports; a coding environment with file access
outcome: A clickable HTML prototype with realistic data and a visible version.

Save a browser-runnable entry at prototype/index.html and explain any build step required by the actual components. Flag missing components instead of silently substituting a different design system.

steps.title: Capture the handoff method
steps.prompt: Document the component mapping, data fixtures, wrapper structure, and testing steps so another designer can reproduce this prototype workflow.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare a reviewable version
steps.prompt: Add a small version stamp and package the prototype for review. Return the local runnable files; create a hosted preview only if a publishing tool and destination are available.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Plan updates from specification changes

steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Prototype a playable browser game
summary: Build and playtest the core loop before expanding the game.
prerequisites: Provide the game concept, controls, target devices, and a runnable development repository.
outcome: A playable browser game with run instructions and a record of playtest results.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Plan and build a browser game about [concept] in this repository. Define the core loop, controls, win or loss conditions, and first playable scope in a short plan. Create the required visuals and implement the game with a coherent interface. Keep a work log as you iterate. Run it in a real browser, play the complete loop, and inspect input handling, restart behavior, and layout on the target devices. Fix observed problems and return the run command, playtest evidence, and known limitations.

title: Pursue a goal with a verifiable finish
summary: Keep a complex task organized around evidence of completion.
prerequisites: Define the objective, allowed scope, resource limits, and an observable completion condition; long-running execution needs a suitable agent.
outcome: A persistent progress record and completion evidence for the agreed objective.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Work toward [objective] until [verifiable end state] is achieved within [scope and resource limits]. Establish the starting state, break the work into concrete milestones, and record decisions, evidence, and unresolved issues so the task can resume reliably. Validate each milestone against the intended outcome. If a required input or capability is missing, identify the exact blocker and continue independent work where useful. Do not describe partial progress as completion or claim that background execution continues when the environment cannot support it.

steps.title: Check progress against the goal
steps.prompt: Compare the current result with the agreed end state. Identify the remaining gap, the next action most likely to close it, and the evidence that would establish completion.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

summary: Match transactions across statements and accounting records, then document what needs correction.

outcome: An annotated reconciliation and reviewable correcting entries.

steps.title: Match and explain
steps.prompt: Reconcile [period] using the attached bank statement, ledger, and chart of accounts. Show matched transactions, timing differences, uncategorized items, duplicates, and unexplained amounts, with source references. Draft correcting entries only where the evidence supports them, using valid account IDs, and explain the effect of every adjustment.

steps.title: Export the reviewed entries
steps.prompt: Export these reviewed adjustments: [entry IDs] as a CSV in [accounting-system format]. Verify balanced entries and prepare a reconciliation summary showing starting balances, differences, adjustments, and final tie-out. Identify recurring recording problems by expense category.

summary: Match people and cost centers to uncover planning and accounting differences.

Consistent reporting date and definitions of employee, contractor, and budgeted position
outcome: A cost-center reconciliation with categorized exceptions and source references.

steps.title: Reconcile the headcount
steps.prompt: Reconcile [month] headcount across the HR roster, approved plan, and payroll/GL records using employee ID and cost center. Identify unplanned hires, budgeted vacancies, roster records with no payroll, payroll records absent from HR, and contractors classified as employees. Explain effective-date and timing differences separately. Produce a cost-center reconciliation and an exception list linked to the source rows.

steps.title: Save reconciliation rules
steps.prompt: Document the matching keys, cost-center mapping, headcount definitions, timing treatment, and exception categories. Incorporate my corrections into the repeatable review process.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the monthly refresh
steps.prompt: Define a check for a new HR export in [close folder], reconciling it with the corresponding plan and payroll period. Save a dated result without overwriting prior reconciliations; recurring execution requires the appropriate source access and scheduler.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Reconcile intercompany balances and draft adjustments
summary: Match both entities' ledgers, isolate genuine breaks, and prepare supported journal-entry drafts.

NetSuite and Microsoft 365 can supply live ledger data and Excel editing; set rounding and materiality thresholds.
outcome: A reconciliation workbook with tie-outs and balanced draft entries.

steps.title: Reconcile the ledgers
steps.prompt: Reconcile [period]'s intercompany balances across these entities. Convert using the supplied FX policy and rates, match references and amounts with visible confidence, and classify differences as timing, rounding, or genuine breaks. Do not force uncertain matches. For each substantiated break, draft balanced debits and credits with account, memo, and supporting reference, and include workbook tie-outs.

steps.title: Review the exceptions
steps.prompt: Show unmatched items, low-confidence pairs, and adjustments above [materiality]. Explain why each proposed entry resolves the break, verify debit-credit balance, and prepare the approved upload format as a draft without posting entries.

title: Refactor a large SwiftUI screen
summary: Clarify view boundaries and state ownership while preserving behavior.
prerequisites: Provide the SwiftUI screen, related models/services, and an Xcode build or test environment.
outcome: A smaller, readable view structure with documented state flow and parity checks.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Refactor [SwiftUI screen] without changing its appearance, navigation, or behavior. Organize properties, computed state, body, helpers, and actions clearly. Extract meaningful subviews with small explicit inputs, bindings, and callbacks. Move complex side effects out of the view body and business logic into the existing model or service layer. Prefer the appropriate native state and environment mechanisms over an unnecessary new view-model abstraction. Keep the root view tree stable and correct observable-state ownership. Build or test after each extraction and report the boundaries, data flow, and parity evidence.

Spreadsheet editing; NetSuite or document-store access or exported files
outcome: A four-quarter model and a one-page leadership assumptions memo.

Build base, upside, and downside cases using explicit input changes. Save a new workbook copy with separate scenario tabs and working formulas alongside the supplied original; preserve the original unchanged. List every changed assumption and its magnitude, and show the impact on key outputs. Write a one-page plain-language memo explaining what drives the scenario differences and save it beside the new workbook.

steps.title: Save the forecasting method
steps.prompt: Document the driver relationships, input sources, scenario sensitivities, reconciliation checks, and memo structure as reusable instructions.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the reforecast cadence
steps.prompt: Define a process that detects newly closed actuals in [forecast folder], creates a refreshed model and scenario memo, and preserves the prior version. Specify the file, spreadsheet, and scheduling capabilities needed for a recurring run.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

outcome: An editable reporting deck with source tie-outs, visual checks, and review flags.

Identify the common story across workstreams, then update metrics, deltas, charts, risks, milestones, and decisions. Preserve the deck's visual system. Trace significant numbers to source files and flag figures that do not reconcile or require owner confirmation. Render the finished slides and correct overflow, clipping, and layout issues. Deliver the editable presentation and a short list of changes and leadership review points; do not share it.

steps.title: Review changes

steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Refresh a strategic account plan
summary: Bring new account evidence into a coherent deal strategy.

outcome: A refreshed strategy pack with a stakeholder map and grounded next actions.

steps.prompt: Update the strategy for [account] using the supplied CRM records, conversations, usage evidence, customer needs, company context, and prior plan. Produce a stakeholder map, discovery-gap list, risk and objection analysis, value hypothesis, supporting proof points, and next-best actions. Explain what changed from the previous plan. Label stale evidence and assumptions needing account-owner confirmation. Keep the plan as a draft; do not update the CRM or contact the customer.

steps.title: Turn the plan into action

steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

Preserve the original and show each changed assumption. Build base, downside, and upside cases with consistent driver definitions. Explain cash effects, hiring implications, sensitivities, trigger points, and major risks. Include a sensitivity table and identify assumptions requiring approval before the forecast is shared. steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

Focus on material progress and changes, blockers, dependencies, decisions needed, and the next actions with supported owners. Identify stale items that need confirmation. Link important claims to evidence and distinguish inferred status from explicit updates. Return a reviewable brief without editing the project tracker or sending it.

steps.title: Compare reporting periods
steps.prompt: Show what changed between [previous period] and [current period]: completed milestones, shifted dates, resolved or new blockers, and changed decisions. Exclude unchanged background.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

Check units, exclusions, paired observations, and multiplicity, and distinguish true discrepancies from rounding or insufficient information.

steps.title: Verify and explain the issues
steps.prompt: Check [figure] against the source data, including axes, error-bar definitions, and plotted values. Recheck every suspected discrepancy before drafting constructive reviewer comments that state the evidence, its implications, and the clarification or correction needed.

summary: Observe the actual failing interaction before changing the code.

Build and launch the app, inspect the current screen, and execute the reported taps, typing, scrolling, or swipes. Prefer accessibility identifiers and refresh the UI snapshot when layout changes. Capture screenshots, logs, and relevant debugger evidence. Diagnose the cause before making the smallest fix, then repeat the same interaction path. Report the reproduction, code change, environment, and verification gaps.

steps.title: Choose a sharper angle

outcome: Platform-specific drafts with a consistent brand voice.

steps.prompt: Repurpose [source article] into a LinkedIn carousel, a short social thread, a five-email nurture sequence, podcast talking points, and an infographic outline. Use the supplied brand examples to maintain a recognizable voice while adapting structure and length to each channel. Present everything in one navigable review document and supply separate files for each format.

steps.title: Simplify the carousel

outcome: A one-page account brief with three relevant conversation openers.

Return a document suitable for the account folder.

steps.prompt: Turn the research approach and my feedback into reusable account-research instructions. Define the sources, freshness checks, one-page structure, and account-folder naming convention.
