title: Resolve a reported vulnerability
summary: Turn an accepted external or internal finding into a minimal, testable remediation.
prerequisites: Provide the report, affected component, expected security invariant, proof, and repository access.
outcome: A focused remediation with reproduction evidence and regression coverage.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Fix [accepted security finding] from [report or ticket]. Review the attacker-controlled input, broken control, expected invariant, and existing proof. Confirm the issue still exists when feasible; if it is already fixed, show the evidence. Make the smallest change that restores the invariant, add a focused regression check, and verify both the original failure and legitimate behavior. Keep unrelated findings and refactors out of scope. Return changed files, commands, results, and any remaining uncertainty without merging or deploying.

title: Review a contract against the playbook
summary: Classify clause deviations and draft fallback language using your established standards.
prerequisites: Contract draft, approved playbook, fallback positions, and deal context
Document editing; Ironclad, Microsoft 365, iManage, or NetDocuments access if connected
outcome: A clause-level risk table and reviewable redlines.

steps.title: Review each clause
steps.prompt: Compare the attached MSA clause by clause with our approved contract playbook. Mark each clause green, yellow, or red against the stated standard and explain the deviation briefly. For yellow or red items, propose replacement language and a concise rationale for opposing counsel. Cite the original clause and relevant playbook rule, and flag matters the playbook does not resolve.

steps.title: Incorporate reviewer feedback
steps.prompt: Update the review method and fallback language using my feedback. Preserve the distinction between approved policy and a proposed exception.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Compare negotiation rounds
steps.prompt: Compare the latest counterparty draft with the previous reviewed version. Update the clause table and add a short change summary showing which issues were resolved, introduced, or remain open.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the contract intake routine
steps.prompt: Define a weekday review workflow for new files in [contract intake folder], producing a clause table and proposed redlines per counterparty. Specify the required document access and schedule rather than claiming a background process is already running.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Review a pull request for regressions
summary: Find consequential behavior changes, security risks, and missing coverage.
prerequisites: Provide the pull request or exact diff and repository context.
outcome: Severity-ranked findings with code references and verification gaps.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review [pull request or diff] against its base revision. Focus on regressions, security-relevant behavior changes, data loss, and tests that fail to cover the changed contract. Trace affected callers and error paths before raising a finding. For each actionable issue, explain the concrete trigger, impact, and relevant file and line. Put findings first by severity. State what was verified and which checks were not run. If no issues are supported by evidence, say so without implying the change is fully proven safe.

title: Review an earnings release against your model
summary: Locate forecast misses and distinguish management guidance from your own assumptions before editing.
prerequisites: Connect S&P Global and provide the valuation workbook and previous presentation.
Workbook edits and slide construction require Excel and PowerPoint editing tools or connected add-ins.
outcome: A cell-referenced earnings brief, scenario tab, and investment-meeting page.

steps.title: Flag the model implications
steps.prompt: Retrieve [company and period]'s earnings release and call transcript, then compare reported figures with my workbook. Identify material forecast differences and assumptions the commentary does not support. Produce a brief listing exact sheet and cell references, proposed changes, evidence, and uncertainty before editing. Treat explanations for the share-price reaction as hypotheses unless verified.

steps.title: Build reviewed scenarios
steps.prompt: For these reviewed assumptions: [cells and decisions], update the workbook and build best, base, and worst scenarios in a new tab. Preserve an audit of changed cells and sources, then create a presentation page explaining the result without implying management endorsed our out-year assumptions.

title: Review and clean a financial workbook
summary: Fix clear spreadsheet defects while preserving business assumptions.
prerequisites: Attach the financial model, priority tabs, expected outputs, and source references.
outcome: A cleaned workbook and severity-ranked QA memo with exact cell references.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review [financial model] before it goes to [audience]. Inspect formulas, hardcodes, broken links, circular references, sign conventions, periods, source tie-outs, checks, and presentation tabs, focusing on [priority areas]. Work on a copy. Correct formatting and formula defects only where the intended behavior is clear; do not alter business assumptions without approval. Deliver the cleaned editable workbook and a severity-ranked memo showing issues, fixes, unresolved assumptions, and cells requiring finance-owner review.

steps.title: Verify the cleanup
steps.prompt: Compare the cleaned workbook with the original. Confirm that approved assumptions are unchanged, explain every material output difference, and rerun the relevant tie-outs and model checks.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Review assessment scoring consistency
summary: Surface rubric ambiguities and evidence for faculty calibration.
prerequisites: Provide de-identified submissions, rubric, grading export, sample feedback, and calibration rules.
outcome: A calibration workbook with sourced flags and faculty review questions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review the de-identified assessment evidence for [course or assignment]. Compare rubric use and feedback patterns across the supplied samples. Flag possible scoring inconsistencies with specific evidence, summarize common strengths and gaps, and identify unclear rubric language. Create a calibration workbook that helps faculty investigate the flags and discuss a common interpretation. Do not assign, revise, or recommend individual grades; leave scoring judgments to the educators.

title: Review course engagement patterns
summary: Make completion gaps and data questions visible for faculty review.
prerequisites: Provide de-identified LMS, attendance, gradebook, assignment, calendar, and metric-definition data.
outcome: A faculty-facing dashboard and evidence-based review queue.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Analyze the supplied de-identified course activity and assessment data. Show engagement trends, completion gaps, assessment patterns, and changes over the course calendar. Check missing or inconsistent data and make metric definitions explicit. Create a dashboard and a faculty review queue that links each concern to the supporting evidence. Avoid diagnosing students or inferring personal circumstances. Do not automate outreach, grades, placement, or support decisions; leave interpretation and action to the faculty.

title: Review promotional email clutter
summary: Find low-value automated mail while keeping personal and important messages out of the cleanup list.
prerequisites: Gmail access through a browser or mail connector; an export supports review only
Your company domain and senders that should always be retained
outcome: A sender-grouped review list and an optional approved cleanup.

steps.title: Find cleanup candidates
steps.prompt: Review my inbox for retailer promotions, inactive newsletters, expired notifications, completed delivery updates, and SaaS marketing. Exclude personal correspondence, attachments, and messages from [company domain]. Group candidates by sender with counts and the reason each group qualifies. Do not delete anything; provide a reviewable list. Do not infer unopened status if the available mail data cannot establish it.

steps.title: Apply the reviewed selection
steps.prompt: Keep [approved exceptions]. Delete only the remaining messages from the reviewed candidate list, using the available mail tool. Report which actions succeeded and any messages that could not be changed.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Reduce future clutter
steps.prompt: For promotional senders with more than [15] messages in the reviewed list, identify their unsubscribe options and unsubscribe from the senders I approve. Do not treat unsubscribing as deleting existing mail.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Find recurring charges
steps.prompt: Identify recurring-payment and renewal emails. List the service, amount, renewal date if stated, and supporting message so I can review subscriptions separately.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Review recent spending and subscriptions
summary: See cash patterns and unusual activity from verified account data.
prerequisites: Provide approved account connections or statements covering the last 30 days.
outcome: A read-only financial overview with source coverage and items to investigate.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review my finances for the last 30 days using [approved accounts or statements]. Summarize spending, saving, account balances, balance changes, recurring bills, and subscriptions. Identify unusual transactions or amounts with the evidence needed for me to investigate. Separate transfers between my own accounts from expenses where the data allows. State the period and accounts covered and flag missing or stale balances. Keep this read-only; do not move money, cancel services, or make investment transactions.

steps.title: Inspect recurring charges
steps.prompt: List recurring charges and upcoming renewals supported by the data. Show amount, frequency, most recent occurrence, and any unexplained increase. Mark uncertain recurrence rather than treating it as confirmed.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Review security from the command line
summary: Choose the right revision and scope, then inspect both findings and coverage.
prerequisites: Requires an authorized local checkout, installed security CLI, authentication, and repository security documents.
outcome: A reproducible local review with exact scope and evidence locations.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prepare a command-line security review of [working changes, branch diff, or selected component]. Verify the intended checkout and full revisions. For a branch review, compare the proposed head to its merge base; for local work, include only the intended staged and unstaged changes. Supply the repository policy and architecture context. Keep a selected-path assessment separate from a diff review, and include consumers of changed shared code where needed. Run the approved command, then inspect the manifest, findings, and coverage. Report commands, target revisions, unresolved alerts, and incomplete areas.

title: Review shipped interfaces for design-system drift
summary: Check UI screenshots and code changes against tokens, components, and interaction rules.
prerequisites: Design-system tokens, component documentation, interaction patterns, and approved exceptions
Shipped screenshots and UI pull requests; GitHub/Figma access or exports
outcome: A severity-ranked drift report with specific system-compliant fixes.

steps.title: Find system deviations
steps.prompt: Review the supplied shipped screens and open UI pull requests against our design system. Report deviations in tokens, component use, spacing, and interaction behavior. For each finding, cite the screen or code location, expected rule, severity, and a practical compliant fix. Exclude matching patterns and approved exceptions; do not infer unobserved interactions from a still image.

steps.title: Capture the review standard
steps.prompt: Update reusable review instructions with the component map, token sources, severity definitions, and approved exception list, incorporating my corrections.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Track unresolved drift
steps.prompt: Create a shareable report with a running count of open high-severity items. Distinguish new, fixed, unchanged, and unverified findings.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare recurring UI review
steps.prompt: Define a review of new UI-labeled pull requests and screenshots at 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on weekdays. Draft findings for the appropriate review surface; automatic commenting requires repository/channel write access and scheduling support.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Review single-cell RNA sequencing quality
summary: Choose justified cell filters and inspect annotation patterns without losing raw counts.
prerequisites: Provide a 10x-style count-matrix bundle, sample manifest, dataset metadata, and an analysis runtime.
outcome: A filtered h5ad file, QC tables, threshold plots, and a review summary.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Inspect the supplied single-cell count matrix, manifest, and metadata. Choose quality-control thresholds from the observed distributions rather than applying unexplained defaults. Preserve raw counts. Report the cells removed or flagged by each filter, show plots that justify the thresholds, and generate global and group-level UMAP views for review. Return the filtered h5ad dataset and a concise summary of quality issues, annotation uncertainty, and decisions that require scientific review. Do not imply that an attractive embedding validates the underlying labels.

title: Review underwriting assumptions before drafting a credit memo
summary: Trace ratios and policy exceptions to statements and workbook cells before making changes.
prerequisites: Borrower statements, peer data, underwriting workbook, policy thresholds, and credit-memo template
S&P Global access or exports; spreadsheet editing that preserves formulas; a document editor or file export capability for the credit memo
outcome: An exception-led credit brief, scenario analysis, and memo draft.

steps.title: Review the credit first
steps.prompt: Review [borrower and facility] before changing the underwriting workbook. Reconcile three years of financial statements and peer data with the existing spread. Identify policy breaches, inconsistent assumptions, and unsupported inputs. For every proposed change, give the worksheet/cell, statement reference, current value, suggested value, and reason. Lead with the exception list and leave the model unchanged until reviewed.

steps.title: Test covenant headroom
steps.prompt: Explain the fixed-charge coverage calculation and its relevant cells. Model revenue at plus/minus 5% and the lease assumption at plus/minus 100 basis points. Compare our growth assumption with borrower guidance and show the base/downside effect without overwriting the original case.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Compare the prior review
steps.prompt: Explain changes since the previous review in leverage, coverage, and working capital, using comparable definitions and source-backed figures.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Challenge management assumptions
steps.prompt: Check [growth assumption] against the borrower's latest pipeline narrative. Separate stated guidance, supporting evidence, and our underwriting judgment.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Build the downside and memo
steps.prompt: After the base case is reviewed and approved, create a new downside tab with revenue down 10%, gross margin down 200 basis points, and operating expenses held flat. Preserve the approved base case. Show when covenants fail, then draft and export the credit summary and exceptions section in the supplied memo template.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Review vendor risk against your own framework
summary: Read security evidence and contract terms together to identify material gaps and mitigations.
prerequisites: Provide the SOC 2 report, security questionnaire, DPA, MSA, and vendor-risk framework.
Connect Drive, Microsoft 365, or Box as needed; Ironclad is optional for signed-contract verification.
outcome: A cited risk memo with a go/no-go recommendation and accountable mitigation list.

steps.title: Assess the vendor
steps.prompt: Evaluate this vendor's security and contractual packet against our risk criteria and intended data access. Cite the document and section for every finding, reconcile contradictions between the questionnaire and independent evidence, and identify missing or stale materials. Recommend go, conditional go, or no-go under our framework, with required mitigations and proposed owners for human approval.

steps.title: Make the mitigation plan
steps.prompt: Prioritize unresolved findings by our risk tier and blocking criteria. For each, define the evidence or contract change needed, the responsible function, a target date, and the condition for closure. Keep unverified assurances separate from completed mitigations.

title: Revise a lesson package consistently
summary: Apply reviewed feedback across connected teaching files with version history.
prerequisites: Provide the approved lesson package, specific feedback, and the list of editable files.
outcome: An aligned revised lesson package with archived versions and a change log.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Apply [feedback] to the approved lesson package. First propose a file-by-file change plan for the deck, teacher guide, student handout, and answer key. After approval, update only those files, archive the previous versions, and check that examples, instructions, timing, and answers still agree across the package. Return a concise change log and unresolved questions. Do not alter material outside the approved list.

title: Run a deep repository security assessment
summary: Use repeated investigation passes to reduce missed vulnerabilities and clarify coverage.
prerequisites: Requires authorized repository access, a security-capable code agent, and an explicit assessment scope.
outcome: A consolidated security report with validated findings and remaining proof gaps.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Perform a deep security assessment of [repository or exact folder]. Read the security policy and preserve the agreed scope. Use independent discovery passes across relevant surfaces, consolidate duplicates, and validate the strongest candidates against their actual source-to-impact paths. Keep evidence and coverage records for each pass. Report surviving findings, realistic exploit prerequisites, reviewed areas, exclusions, and proof gaps. Distinguish this repository-wide assessment from a pull-request diff review. Do not apply fixes or imply that incomplete coverage establishes security.

title: Run a focused intake for a new role
summary: Turn a hiring manager's answers into a specific role specification and a clear recruiter handoff.
prerequisites: Provide the role-spec template, leveling guide, and team charter.
Connect Drive, Slack, or Microsoft 365 if the current materials live there.
outcome: A completed role spec with measurable success criteria and open hiring questions.

steps.title: Interview the hiring manager
steps.prompt: Help me scope [new role]. Ask about ownership, essential versus desirable capabilities, seniority, reporting line, and what success at day 90 looks like. Challenge vague requirements until they become observable. Use my answers and our leveling guide to complete the attached role-spec template, then list decisions still needed from the recruiter.

steps.title: Check the role definition
steps.prompt: Review the draft for inconsistent level expectations, unnecessary must-haves, and outcomes that cannot be measured. Propose corrections and produce a short recruiter brief separating settled requirements from unresolved compensation, location, or process questions.

title: Run a focused repository security review
summary: Assess a defined code scope and report realistic risks with evidence.
prerequisites: Requires an authorized repository, security guidance, and a code-capable environment.
outcome: A security report covering findings, proof, exclusions, and gaps.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Assess [repository or scoped folder] for security vulnerabilities. I am authorized to review this code. Read its security policy and architecture context, stay inside the named scope, and use supported validation methods. Trace plausible findings to affected code and realistic impact. Separate validated issues from unresolved suspicions. Report severity, evidence, assumptions, reviewed surfaces, exclusions, and remaining coverage gaps. Prioritize the findings and uncertainties that need human review. Do not apply patches or close findings during this assessment.

steps.title: Understand one finding
steps.prompt: Explain [finding] from attacker-controlled input to the broken security boundary. Identify the prerequisites, evidence that supports the impact, and the smallest validation needed to resolve uncertainty.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Run a workflow with item-level evidence
summary: Normalize inputs, execute approved work, and verify every result.
prerequisites: Provide inputs, approval or policy source, runner, scope, and expected verification artifact.
outcome: A per-item success/failure ledger with retries and verification evidence.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Run [workflow] on [approved inputs] using [runner]. Inspect required fields and normalize dates, amounts, owners, and identifiers before execution. Use a dry run where supported. Execute only the approved scope, recording one success or failure result per item. Retry transient failures once without repeating completed work. Verify outcomes using [result file, log, dashboard, or screenshot]. Summarize totals, retries, failures, and evidence locations. Pause before irreversible actions or any expansion of scope.

steps.title: Capture the repeatable procedure
steps.prompt: Turn the verified run into reusable instructions covering inputs, normalization, dry run, item identity, retry rules, and evidence checks. Include the observed failure modes and how to recover without repeating successful actions.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Scaffold a desktop-native macOS app
summary: Set up Mac scenes, commands, and a simple local build-and-run workflow.
prerequisites: Requires macOS, Xcode or Swift tooling, and the app brief or existing project.
outcome: A runnable Mac app slice with reusable development commands.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Create or extend a SwiftUI macOS app for [purpose]. Choose a main-window scene and add Settings, menu-bar, or utility windows only when they serve the workflow. Prefer native sidebars, menus, toolbars, keyboard shortcuts, and system materials. Use xcodebuild for an Xcode project or swift build for a package-based app and add a project-local build-and-run script. Keep AppKit bridging narrow and explain its need. Exercise the feature after each meaningful change and return exact verification commands and desktop-specific follow-ups.

title: Schedule private meeting prep and a weekly recap
summary: Use your calendar, messages, and documents to prepare for meetings and close the week with a forwardable recap.
prerequisites: Requires a private-message assistant with scheduled routines.
Connect your own Google Calendar, Gmail, and Drive, or Microsoft 365; workspace search supplies relevant chat threads.
Set your timezone and routine times.
outcome: Recurring private prep notes and a draft weekly progress recap.

steps.title: Set the morning briefing
steps.prompt: Every weekday at [time and timezone], send me a private note for each meeting on today's calendar. Include attendees, outstanding commitments, relevant documents, recent correspondence, and one useful question to ask. Link the evidence and flag anything that may have changed since the note was generated.

steps.title: Add the Friday recap
steps.prompt: Every Friday at [time and timezone], draft a private recap I can forward: completed work, delayed commitments and reasons, messages awaiting my response, and next week's earliest deadlines. Keep this as a draft. Also list the routines you now have configured and their next run times.

title: Scope an ambiguous analytics request
summary: Translate a stakeholder question into a defensible analysis and first answer.
prerequisites: Provide the original request, relevant context, metric definitions, and available data sources.
outcome: An analysis plan, first-pass result, and a list of decisions still needed.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Turn [stakeholder request] into a concrete analysis. Define the decision to support, business question, relevant metrics, required data, join logic, and scope. Identify unclear definitions before calculating. Run a first pass only where the available data supports it, validate outputs, and prepare a concise answer with charts, caveats, and sources. List every missing input or unresolved decision that prevents a final conclusion. Do not assume missing values or silently choose conflicting metric definitions.

steps.title: Respond to the requester
steps.prompt: Draft a short stakeholder response with the provisional answer, what can be concluded now, and the few clarifications that would materially improve the analysis. Keep it as a draft.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Score pipeline health for the weekly review
summary: Surface stalled opportunities and weak next steps using your own stage criteria.
prerequisites: Connect Salesforce and Drive, or attach the current pipeline export.
Provide stage-exit criteria, risk thresholds, and the previous review.
outcome: A scored pipeline sheet and a meeting-ready risk narrative.

steps.title: Inspect open opportunities
steps.prompt: Evaluate every open opportunity in [period] against our stage-exit requirements, evidence of a concrete next step, and time spent in stage. Produce a scored sheet with source links and a one-line explanation for each at-risk deal. Compare with the last review and write the manager briefing for our pipeline meeting.

steps.title: Turn risk into action
steps.prompt: For the highest-priority risks, state what evidence is missing, the next customer or internal action, its owner, and when the team should reassess. Separate genuine deal movement from administrative stage updates.

title: Specify a dashboard that supports decisions
summary: Define metrics, views, ownership, and monitoring before building.
prerequisites: Provide the business question, workflow, metric definitions, source examples, and stakeholder needs.
outcome: A buildable dashboard specification with validation and ownership rules.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Design a dashboard specification for [workflow or decision]. Use the supplied strategy, data exports, metric definitions, existing examples, and feedback. Explain the decisions it should enable, the KPI hierarchy, each calculation, chart, and filter, and the data needed. Define quality checks, acceptance checks, owners, handoffs, and a monitoring approach. Highlight access and publication constraints. Do not invent a metric definition or call the design production-ready before its sources and calculations are validated.

steps.title: Define actionable alerts
steps.prompt: For each proposed monitored metric, specify the threshold or comparison, owner, required context, and expected response. Remove alerts that have no useful decision or reliable source behind them.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Standardize repeat contract reviews
summary: Capture a legal team's playbook and commenting style in a persistent review workspace.
prerequisites: Upload the review playbook, preferred template, unacceptable-terms list, and sample reviews.
Requires a project workspace with persistent reference files; document generation is needed for the guide.
outcome: A standards guide and reusable project instructions, calibrated on completed reviews.

steps.title: Create the standards
steps.prompt: Analyze our attached contract-review materials. Produce a review standards guide covering preferred terms, prohibited positions, severity definitions, escalation triggers, and our issue-risk-recommendation comment style. Draft reusable project instructions that require the guide on each review and distinguish missing guidance from established policy.

steps.title: Calibrate against real reviews
steps.prompt: Review these previously assessed agreements using the new guide, then compare your findings with our completed reviews. Identify missed issues, severity disagreements, and tone differences. Revise the instructions based on the documented corrections and leave unresolved policy questions for counsel.

title: Stress-test a fundraising campaign goal
summary: Translate a campaign target into gift tiers, prospect requirements, and cultivation pressure.
prerequisites: Provide the campaign target, known lead-gift ceiling, prospect pipeline, and historical conversion rates where available.
Requires interactive visualization support for a goal slider.
outcome: An adjustable gift pyramid with visible prospect gaps.

steps.title: Build the gift pyramid
steps.prompt: For a campaign target of [amount], model gift tiers and the number of gifts and qualified prospects required at each level. Make the goal adjustable. Use our historical conversion rates when supplied; label any planning ratios as assumptions. Compare requirements with our actual prospect list and flag gaps without inventing a typical pipeline for us.

steps.title: Test feasibility
steps.prompt: Cap the lead gift at [amount] and redistribute the remaining target. Show which tiers now carry more pressure, then add realistic cultivation stages and timing from our pipeline to test whether a [duration]-month campaign is plausible.

title: Stress-test a long-term financial plan
summary: Model how earnings changes, inflation, taxes, and withdrawal timing interact over time.
prerequisites: Provide account statements, tax returns, benefits estimates, expenses, ages, and goals.
Requires spreadsheet modeling and current jurisdiction-specific tax information; review consequential strategies with a qualified adviser.
outcome: An adjustable scenario workbook with assumptions and questions for professional review.

steps.title: Find where the plan breaks
steps.prompt: Using these documents and goals, build a year-by-year financial model connecting income, spending, account types, debt payoff, benefits timing, taxes, and withdrawals. Test adverse return sequences, inflation, and employment changes. Make assumptions adjustable and distinguish simulated outcomes from guarantees. Identify which uncertainties most affect feasibility and which decisions need a financial or tax professional's review.

steps.title: Trace a life change
steps.prompt: Model this change: [income loss, retirement date, expense, or inflation shock]. Recalculate its effects on saving, tax brackets, conversion windows, and withdrawal order. Compare with the baseline and show the assumptions that drive the difference rather than recommending a transaction from one scenario.

title: Sweep messages across your work apps
summary: Combine unread conversations into topics, decide what needs attention, and prepare concise replies.
prerequisites: Connect Slack, Microsoft 365 for Teams, and Gmail, or provide recent message exports.
A scheduler and a writable notes folder are needed only for recurring saved sweeps.
outcome: One topic-based inbox roundup with short reply drafts.

steps.title: Group the unread work
steps.prompt: Review my unread direct messages, mentions, Teams activity, and email from the past [24 hours]. Combine messages about the same subject across apps. For each topic, label it Reply needed, Read carefully, or FYI, name the people involved, and link the original messages. Draft a response of at most three sentences for each topic that needs me.

steps.title: Tune the next sweep
steps.prompt: Use these priority senders and channels: [list]. Apply these exclusions: [rules]. Revise the roundup, flag uncertain context, and save this sorting pattern so later sweeps follow the same rules. Keep replies as drafts.

title: Synthesize interview evidence for a debrief
summary: Show where interviewers agree, where evidence conflicts, and what the panel must resolve.
prerequisites: Completed interviewer scorecards, role rubric, and competency expectations
Authorized access to candidate material; no automated hiring decision is requested
outcome: A neutral debrief brief with competency coverage and three decision questions.

steps.title: Prepare the panel brief
steps.prompt: Synthesize the supplied interview scorecards against the role rubric. Show where the panel agrees and disagrees, distinguish strong behavioral evidence from anecdotes, and identify competencies that were not assessed. Cite the relevant scorecard evidence and propose three questions to resolve in the debrief. Do not recommend hire/no-hire or infer protected characteristics; the decision stays with the panel.

steps.title: Refine the synthesis rules
steps.prompt: Document our rubric, convergence criteria, evidence standard, and missing-coverage flags. Apply my feedback while preserving the separation between evidence synthesis and the panel's judgment.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare complete-scorecard intake
steps.prompt: Define a weekday 9 a.m. check for candidates whose required scorecards are complete. Create a brief in the relevant role folder, preserving access limits and avoiding duplicate drafts. Scheduling requires connected tools.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Synthesize user interviews into research findings
summary: Group observations into clear themes while preserving participant evidence and open questions.
prerequisites: Provide all transcripts, discussion guide, and participant roster.
Airtable and Drive can supply study context; Miro or an artifact tool is optional for shared visual synthesis.
outcome: A research readout with attributed evidence and changes since the previous round.

steps.title: Write the findings
steps.prompt: Read the interview set for [study]. Organize observations into roughly five to seven plainly named themes, with two or three short supporting quotations identified by participant and source location. Distinguish observed behavior from interpretation, include important counterexamples, and end with unanswered research questions. Keep participant identity handling consistent with the supplied roster.

steps.title: Update with new interviews
steps.prompt: Incorporate these additional transcripts and explain which themes strengthened, weakened, split, or disappeared. Add a concise change note and retain the evidence trail so the team can tell real new insight from relabeling.

title: Test the app as a real user
summary: Exercise important flows and capture actionable reproduction details.
prerequisites: Provide the test environment, approved account or fixtures, and the critical user flows.
outcome: A prioritized bug report with expected and actual results.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Test [application or environment] through these user journeys: [flows]. Navigate the real interface, including relevant forms, empty states, and transitions. For each failure, record reproducible steps, expected behavior, actual behavior, severity, and useful screenshots or logs. Continue past non-blocking issues so the review covers all requested flows. Finish with a triage summary and state what could not be tested. Use only the approved test data and avoid consequential production actions.

title: Track customer account health
summary: Combine usage, support, sentiment, and success-plan progress into one health assessment.
prerequisites: Usage export, open support tickets, NPS responses, and success plan
Salesforce, Zendesk, and Drive access or equivalent exports
outcome: An evidence-backed health rating and two actions for the week.

steps.title: Assess account health
steps.prompt: Review [account] using the attached usage data, open and recently resolved support tickets, NPS feedback, and success plan. Assign a red, yellow, or green health rating with a concise evidence-based explanation. Recommend the two most useful actions this week, naming an owner where the records identify one. Mark missing or stale evidence.

steps.title: Define a repeatable review
steps.prompt: Document the rating criteria, source checks, and summary format as reusable instructions. Incorporate my corrections so the next review applies the same standards.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Review the customer portfolio
steps.prompt: Apply these criteria to each account in [portfolio]. Produce an individual health summary and one digest of red accounts. Prepare the instructions for a Monday 7 a.m. review in [timezone]; only create a recurring task if scheduling is available.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Triage dependency risk in CI
summary: Connect package alerts to reachable code and review dependency updates.
prerequisites: Provide dependency alerts, manifests, lockfiles, CI configuration, and authorized repository access.
outcome: A dependency-risk ledger and a narrowly scoped scan workflow proposal.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Assess [dependency alerts or package update] against this repository. Check the affected versions, whether the vulnerable behavior is reachable, and what evidence supports or weakens each alert. Produce a ledger with validated, unresolved, and ruled-out findings and reasons. Propose a CI check triggered by relevant manifest or lockfile changes. Keep runner credentials isolated, handle untrusted pull requests appropriately, and preserve scan reports even on failure. Do not run package lifecycle scripts or dismiss alerts merely because a scanner completed.

title: Triage escalations and alert people only for critical cases
summary: Apply your severity rules, connect related tickets, and route work without paging everyone.
prerequisites: Requires a proactive channel assistant with write access to Zendesk, Intercom, or Jira Service Management.
Provide severity definitions, ownership rules, and the P1 contact; PagerDuty is optional for incident checks.
outcome: An organized escalation queue with first-response drafts and targeted critical alerts.

steps.title: Set the triage responsibility
steps.prompt: For each new escalation in [channel], apply our severity definitions, compare it with existing tickets, and link or merge verified duplicates according to our support rules. Tag the owning team and draft a first customer response for an agent to review. Alert a person only when the case meets P1 criteria, stating the evidence and decision needed.

steps.title: Review the queue
steps.prompt: Summarize escalations since [time], highlighting [priority category], unresolved owners, and cases requiring a human decision. Apply this correction to [ticket]: [severity or owner correction], and update the channel's rules only where I explicitly request a lasting change.

title: Triage NDAs against your legal playbook
summary: Check standard paper systematically and isolate the clauses that need counsel.
prerequisites: Attach the NDA, your approved mutual template, and your current NDA playbook.
Routing requires a connected document system and an authorized signature workflow such as DocuSign.
outcome: A criterion-by-criterion NDA triage card and exception queue.

steps.title: Apply the NDA checklist
steps.prompt: Compare this NDA with every criterion in our attached playbook. Record Pass, Exception, or Unclear with the clause reference and rationale. Where the agreement departs from our approved position, give counsel a concise exception list. If all criteria pass, prepare it for the approved signature-routing workflow; do not treat missing or ambiguous clauses as passes.

steps.title: Prepare the intake queue
steps.prompt: Apply the same checklist to the remaining NDAs in [intake folder]. Save one triage card per agreement, separate standard drafts from exceptions, and produce a review queue with filenames and clause links. Route only agreements that satisfy the documented approval policy.

title: Triage requests in an IT help channel
summary: Answer from policy, collect missing details, and route unresolved requests to an owner.
prerequisites: IT knowledge base and ownership rules
A channel-connected assistant plus ticketing write access for automated replies and filing; pasted requests support manual triage
outcome: Grounded replies and complete, deduplicated escalation tickets.

steps.title: Define the channel triage workflow
steps.prompt: For each request in [IT help channel], check for an existing duplicate and look for an answer in the connected IT knowledge base. Reply with the relevant policy link or ask for missing details. When an owner's decision is needed, prepare one ticket with the request, context, and correct assignee. Do not grant access or make the approval decision. If channel or ticket access is unavailable, draft the response and ticket from the material I provide.

steps.title: Review routing patterns
steps.prompt: Group the recent requests by recurring issue and owner. Identify unresolved or unrouted items and suggest clarifications to the routing rules.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the weekly digest
steps.prompt: Summarize this week's request count, major themes, and outstanding routing gaps. Include untagged channel messages only if the integration can actually read them. Prepare a Friday 3 p.m. digest in [timezone]; configure recurrence only where scheduling is supported.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Restrict response behavior
steps.prompt: Update the channel instructions so the assistant replies only when directly mentioned. State whether the connected channel supports this setting; otherwise return the exact instruction for the channel administrator.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Triage your inbox and draft replies
summary: Find urgent email, suggest a cleanup, and prepare replies in your voice.
prerequisites: Connect the approved mailbox or provide an email export; include recent sent messages to establish tone.
outcome: A prioritized inbox brief, cleanup proposal, and unsent reply drafts.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review the last 90 days in [mailbox], including recent messages I wrote. Keep separate accounts separate. Identify up to five conversations that need action, with links, timing, and the reason each matters. Check the latest replies before calling a request unresolved. Propose labels and archive candidates without hiding bills, deadlines, security notices, or active conversations. Draft one useful response in my usual tone. End with separate decisions for applying the cleanup and saving the reply. Do not send messages, archive mail, or move anything to Trash until I approve the exact action.

steps.title: Set a review cadence
steps.prompt: Propose an inbox-check schedule for [time zone and working hours] using the priorities we agreed. Include the sources and notification rules in the task instructions. Show the schedule for approval, and confirm whether the platform can actually run it. Report meaningful changes without repeating resolved items.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Turn a bug report into a reviewable draft pull request
summary: Reproduce the issue, implement a focused fix, and connect verification back to the report.
prerequisites: Bug report with reproduction context and access to the affected repository
Coding/test environment and GitHub write access for a draft PR; channel access only for posting updates
outcome: A draft pull request with reproduction evidence, tests, and CI status.

steps.title: Reproduce and fix the report
steps.prompt: In [repository], investigate the bug described in [report or thread]. Reproduce it, identify the cause, implement a focused fix using existing conventions, and add meaningful regression coverage. Open a draft pull request linking the report and explaining validation. Check CI and report its actual status; do not call the work complete while required checks are failing or still running.

steps.title: Apply repository-specific guidance
steps.prompt: Update the fix using [canonical field-definition file] rather than duplicating its values in a constant. Inspect the existing implementation and adjust the regression check to cover the real behavior.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Follow the pull request checks
steps.prompt: Check [pull request] until its current CI run finishes. Report the result and actionable failures here; post to the original thread only if that channel is connected and I have requested the update.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Define bug-triage instructions
steps.prompt: Inspect any existing instructions and routines for [bug channel]. Draft a standing workflow that reproduces each report, opens a draft PR only when the cause is established, and otherwise records what was tried. Identify the repository, channel, ownership, and automation capabilities needed before enabling it.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Investigate without changing code
steps.prompt: For [new report], trace the failure to its cause and explain the evidence and reproduction result. Diagnosis only: do not edit files or create a pull request.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Turn a discussion thread into a code fix
summary: Investigate a reported issue using its conversation context and the correct repository.
prerequisites: Provide the discussion thread, repository, and prepared development environment.
outcome: A minimal fix with checks and a draft response to the original discussion.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Investigate the issue described in [thread] for [repository]. Use the approved development environment and read the repository instructions. Extract the expected behavior and concrete failure evidence from the discussion, inspect the relevant code, and make the smallest supported fix. Run the checks that cover the change and report any reproduction or access gaps. Prepare a concise response explaining the cause, change, and verification. Keep the response as a draft unless I explicitly authorize posting it.

title: Turn a discussion thread into a decision record
summary: Extract the actual agreement, accountable next steps, and unresolved disagreement.
prerequisites: Provide the thread or email chain, or connect Slack and Gmail.
An editable decision log and the team's owner and sign-off conventions are needed for appending records.
outcome: A compact source-linked entry in the team's decision log.

steps.title: Record the decision
steps.prompt: Read [thread or chain]. Write only the established decision, the owner and committed date of each next step, and questions still open or contested. Link each point to its source message. Mark missing owners or dates explicitly, then append a dated entry to [decision log] without turning tentative suggestions into agreements.

steps.title: Check for changes
steps.prompt: Review later replies for corrections or superseding decisions. Update the entry with the changed owner, date, or decision and its source, retaining enough history to explain what changed.

title: Turn a message thread into a researched plan
summary: Read the context behind a request, research workable options, and save a concise reference note.
prerequisites: Requires authorized desktop access to the relevant Messages thread and write access to Apple Notes.
Use current web research for recommendations; provide location, budget, timing, and constraints.
outcome: A sourced plan and practical checklist in your notes app.

steps.title: Research and save the plan
steps.prompt: Read [person or thread] about [event or request] and extract the confirmed requirements. Research options that fit the time, budget, transport, and other constraints. Recommend a practical choice with source links, then save a concise Apple Note with the plan, timing, and a checklist grouped by how I will use it. Use formatting that stays readable on mobile.

steps.title: Update changed requirements
steps.prompt: The thread now says [new information]. Recalculate quantities or timing using the actual change, update the existing note and checklist consistently, and highlight anything that needs confirmation. Draft a reply reflecting the revised plan without sending it.

title: Turn a regulatory change into an action brief
summary: Compare a new rule with your actual products and policies to identify applicable obligations.
prerequisites: Provide current and prior regulatory texts, product descriptions, existing policies, and relevant jurisdictions.
Use authoritative legal research access, such as CoCounsel, and connected Drive or Microsoft 365 where needed.
outcome: A cited applicability brief and an owner-ready action table.

steps.title: Assess the change
steps.prompt: Compare this regulation with the preceding rule and our product and policy documents. For each material change, cite the provision, explain whether and why it appears to apply, identify the policy or product gap, and record the effective date and required action. Flag uncertain applicability for counsel instead of resolving it by assumption.

steps.title: Make the action table
steps.prompt: Turn confirmed gaps into a table with affected product, action, suggested responsible function, deadline, evidence required, and dependency. Separate legal interpretation questions from implementation work and save the brief beside the source materials.

title: Turn a rough voice note into meeting research
summary: Capture an idea on the move and develop it into a sourced argument when you return to your desk.
prerequisites: Provide a rough transcript or use voice input in a conversation that syncs across devices.
Enable web research and access to referenced planning documents; file creation is needed for the final brief.
outcome: A research brief that tests the idea against internal context and counterevidence.

steps.title: Investigate the idea
steps.prompt: Here is my rough idea for [meeting and deadline]: [voice note]. Read [planning document] to recover our priorities, research current examples and evidence, and identify whether the idea is actually supported. Keep unlike metrics separate and cite their definitions and dates. Organize findings into what we know, what remains uncertain, and useful discussion points.

steps.title: Make the meeting brief
steps.prompt: Continue from this research and create a one-page team pre-read with the strongest evidence, concrete examples, and proposed questions. Include the best case against my initial position and explain what additional evidence would change the recommendation.

title: Turn a variance workbook into three executive slides
summary: Explain results, material drivers, and the outlook without burying the audience in detail.
prerequisites: Provide the variance workbook, previous deck, brand template, one-time items, and materiality threshold.
Requires PowerPoint editing with editable charts; Microsoft 365 and Drive can supply the files.
outcome: An editable three-slide deck tied to the underlying financial workbook.

steps.title: Build the three slides
steps.prompt: Create three slides from [period]'s variance workbook using our previous deck layout: result against plan, material drivers, and implications for next period. Show a waterfall for the drivers and separate recurring effects from known one-time items. Reconcile chart values to the workbook, place backup detail in speaker notes, and deliver an editable PPTX.

steps.title: Check the outlook
steps.prompt: Trace each statement about what carries forward to its supporting data or assumption. Flag one-time effects incorrectly treated as recurring, reconcile the bridge to the headline variance, and tighten the notes around the questions leadership is likely to ask.

title: Turn an idea into a working prototype
summary: Explore a visual direction and implement the core user journey.
prerequisites: Provide the idea, audience, main workflow, and a development environment; image generation is optional for visual exploration.
outcome: A working first version with browser-checked interactions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Develop a proof of concept for [idea] aimed at [users]. Define the main workflow and create a visual mockup that makes the direction concrete. Use that reference to implement a focused working version in the available project. Preserve the chosen visual hierarchy and make the primary interaction complete. Check it in a real browser, report what is simulated or missing, and provide the local run instructions.

steps.title: Iterate on feedback
steps.prompt: Apply [specific feedback] to the prototype. Keep the change focused, exercise the affected browser flow, and compare the result with the chosen design before handing it back.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Turn an issue into a tested code change
summary: Tie implementation and review evidence directly to acceptance criteria.
prerequisites: Provide issue, acceptance criteria, exact baseline revision, scoped files, fixtures, and required checks in a prepared environment.
outcome: A minimal diff or authorized draft PR with an acceptance-evidence table.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Implement [issue] in [repository] from [base commit] within [scope]. Read the instructions, relevant code, acceptance criteria, and public contracts. Confirm the revision and run baseline checks; report blocking failures or missing access before implementation. Make the smallest change using existing authorization, error, pagination, and test patterns. Add regression tests that distinguish the new behavior from the old. Run required checks again and map every criterion to actual evidence, with commands, results, revisions, and unrun checks. Return the diff and draft review description, or create a draft PR only when authorized. Do not merge, deploy, alter production, add dependencies, or expand scope without a decision.

steps.title: Verify a cursor-pagination change
steps.instruction: Use this follow-up when the issue changes cursor pagination.
steps.prompt: Verify the pagination contract with fixed fixtures, including tied timestamps across a page boundary, bounded traversal, repeatable cursor replay, and both partial and exactly full final pages. Confirm authorization happens before cursor validation, cover malformed or invalid cursors, and compare successful and error responses with the public schemas. Keep existing assertions strong and update API documentation to match the actual contract. Report any unrun check or unresolved difference explicitly.

title: Turn brand guidelines into a reusable skill
summary: Package visual standards and voice rules into one repeatable workflow for content and design.
prerequisites: Provide brand guidelines, logo assets, exact color and spacing tokens, typography, font fallbacks, and voice examples.
Use exported references or connect the Figma library and the Drive or Notion folder holding the current guidelines.
Creating an installable skill requires file creation and a tool that supports custom skills. Recurring refreshes also require scheduling support.
outcome: A reusable brand skill, verified sample outputs, a one-page team reference, and a documented refresh procedure.

steps.title: Build the brand skill
steps.prompt:
Turn the supplied brand guide, design tokens, and voice examples into a reusable brand skill. Resolve conflicting references by flagging the choice for the brand owner.

Create SKILL.md describing when the skill applies and how to use it. Add reference files for exact colors, typography, spacing, font fallbacks, voice, and prohibited patterns. Cover copy and interfaces as well as presentations, documents, and spreadsheets. Use small helper scripts for repeated formatting where useful; keep editorial and layout decisions in the instructions.

Include a review checklist, accessible contrast checks, and examples of compliant and noncompliant output. Explain why each prohibited choice breaks a rule. If this environment cannot create or install skill files, provide the complete file contents and setup instructions without claiming the skill is installed.

steps.title: Test and refine the rules
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation with the draft skill and the brand references.
steps.prompt: Apply the draft skill to a short quarterly-review deck, a companion spreadsheet, and one interface or copy sample. Check each against the source rules and record specific corrections. Update the skill using this feedback: [changes]. Preserve unaffected standards, explain any remaining brand-owner decisions, and show what changed.

steps.title: Create a team reference
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the test outputs.
steps.prompt: Make a one-page reference for this skill. Show the rules it enforces, examples of good and bad applications, where the source guidelines live, and how a teammate should report an exception. Prepare it for review before publishing or sharing.

steps.title: Keep the skill aligned with the brand
steps.instruction: Use when the source guidelines change. Automatic checks require connected sources and scheduling support.
steps.prompt: Compare the latest brand folder and design-system library against the version used for this skill. Identify changed tokens, voice rules, and examples; update affected files and write a short changelog. Draft a Monday 9 a.m. refresh specification for [timezone], with the sources to check and the owner who reviews conflicts. Do not claim a recurring task is active unless it has actually been configured.

title: Turn engagement feedback into a 30-day action plan
summary: Identify broad employee-survey signals without exposing individual respondents.
prerequisites: Open-text survey export, team/tenure fields, and anonymity rules
Minimum reporting-group thresholds and survey context
outcome: A one-page People brief with three themes and practical short-term actions.

steps.title: Synthesize the survey
steps.prompt: Analyze the open-text engagement responses. Identify the three strongest themes with evidence of breadth rather than relying on the loudest comments. Segment by team and tenure only when the supplied anonymity thresholds allow it. Produce a one-page brief with two or three non-identifying quotes per theme and a draft 30-day action plan. Never attribute a quote to an individual; redact revealing details.

steps.title: Save the analysis rules
steps.prompt: Document our anonymity safeguards, segment thresholds, theme method, and action-plan format. Incorporate my feedback and clearly state what cannot be concluded from the sample.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the next survey cycle
steps.prompt: Define a repeatable process for a new survey export: validate the period, apply the agreed rules, and save the brief and action plans to its cycle folder. A recurring check requires file access and scheduling support.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Turn messages into a ranked action queue
summary: Separate unresolved requests from conversations that have already moved on.
prerequisites: Provide the workstream, time window, and approved direct-message and channel sources.
outcome: A ranked action list with source links and unsent response drafts.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Review messages to me about [workstream] during [period], including direct messages, mentions, and relevant threads. Read the latest replies before deciding that something is unresolved. For each actionable request, state what is needed, whether it requires my reply, an owner, a document or code change, or a decision, why it matters, and the recommended next step. Rank by urgency and impact and link the source. Skip resolved items and prepare drafts without posting them.

steps.title: Draft the responses
steps.prompt: Write concise replies for [selected items], using the latest thread context. Clearly distinguish commitments I have already made from proposed next steps, and keep all messages unsent.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Turn messy invoices into a financial dashboard
summary: Clean invoice records and make monthly trends, client concentration, and aging easy to inspect.
prerequisites: Upload invoice records as CSV or XLSX, including payment status if available.
Requires spreadsheet generation; advanced sparklines may need a library such as xlsxwriter.
outcome: A filterable workbook with reconciled totals, trend charts, and invoice detail.

steps.title: Build the workbook
steps.prompt: Clean this year's invoice data, standardize dates and client names, and preserve the original records in a source tab. Build a restrained financial dashboard with monthly totals, client rankings, sparklines, sortable invoice detail, and frozen headers. Distinguish invoiced amounts from received payments when the data permits. Add comments for ambiguous records and reconcile the dashboard totals to the detail.

steps.title: Add aging and updates
steps.prompt: Add days since invoice and an aging view for unpaid balances. Incorporate these new records without duplicating existing invoices, then refresh charts and totals while preserving the workbook's formatting and formulas.

title: Turn multiple datasets into an answer
summary: Clean, join, and analyze evidence with interpretable charts and limitations.
prerequisites: Attach datasets, define the question, and provide any known join keys or metric definitions.
outcome: A reviewable report or notebook with validated joins and supporting charts.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Answer [research or business question] using the attached datasets. Explain what each file contains, establish valid join keys, and check duplicates, missing fields, unmatched records, and coverage. Preserve original files and do not fill gaps with invented data. Explore the question with clear charts and an interpretable model if needed. Lead the final report with the answer, then explain assumptions, uncertainty, and data problems that could change it. Distinguish association from causation and return the supporting workbook or notebook.

steps.title: Challenge the result
steps.prompt: Check whether the conclusion changes under a reasonable alternative join, outlier treatment, or model specification. Compare the results and explain which assumptions are consequential.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Turn recurring call transcripts into notes and tasks
summary: Give a project-channel assistant a standing job to capture decisions and create accountable follow-up work.
prerequisites: Requires a channel-based assistant that supports standing instructions and proactive replies.
Connect a Zoom, Gong, or Fathom transcript feed and Linear, Jira, or Asana with ticket-write access.
Name the project board and the channel where transcripts arrive.
outcome: Threaded meeting notes, linked tracker tickets, and a maintained decision record.

steps.title: Set the transcript workflow
steps.prompt: For this project channel, process each new call transcript posted by our recorder. Reply in its thread with decisions, unresolved questions, and actions with owners and dates supported by the transcript. Create those actions in [tracker and board], link the tickets, and publish the notes in this channel. Mark missing owners or dates for clarification instead of inventing them.

steps.title: Correct and update the record
steps.prompt: Correct this action: [task] belongs to [owner], with deadline [date]. Update the linked ticket and meeting notes together. Then produce a short decision record explaining the choice made, alternatives rejected, and reasons supported by this conversation.

title: Turn renovation inspiration into a materials plan
summary: Identify the look behind your saved images and compare realistic ways to achieve it.
prerequisites: Upload inspiration images and describe room dimensions, location, budget, and constraints.
Requires image analysis, current product research, and spreadsheet creation.
outcome: A style guide, materials comparison, budget packages, and contractor brief.

steps.title: Translate the inspiration
steps.prompt: Analyze these renovation images and identify the recurring palette, materials, proportions, and details. Research three to five suitable options for each major material category across price tiers in [location]. Build a workbook with cited prices, stated quantities, a style guide, and three formula-driven packages. Explain quality tradeoffs and uncertainty; do not invent resale-return guarantees.

steps.title: Prepare contractor questions
steps.prompt: For the selected package, investigate durability and installation requirements, then create a contractor brief with specifications, sources, budget allocation, fixed requirements, and flexible choices. Map the installation dependencies and show how a [duration] delay to [item] changes the schedule.

title: Turn research into a clear group presentation
summary: Choose the findings that matter and distribute a coherent story across presenters.
prerequisites: Provide the paper, supporting data, assessment rubric, audience, duration, and presenter count.
Canva integration is needed for an editable Canva deck; Drive is optional for source access.
outcome: An editable slide structure and timed speaker notes grounded in the research.

steps.title: Shape the presentation
steps.prompt: Turn this research into a [duration]-minute presentation for [audience] shared by [number] presenters. Select three or four compelling findings, preserve limitations, and build a problem-to-evidence-to-implications narrative. Create an editable Canva deck or detailed slide outline with accurate visual suggestions, plus speaker notes and explicit handoffs. Check chart labels, text fit, and speaking time.

steps.title: Rehearse the hard parts
steps.prompt: Review this practice explanation: [paste]. Flag unclear logic or overstated claims, suggest a better visual for [slide], and ask likely audience questions one at a time so I can practice defending the methods and limitations.

title: Turn strategy notes into a campaign brief
summary: Structure rough marketing decisions into a brief and a kickoff presentation.
prerequisites: Strategy notes, brand guidelines, campaign constraints, and available success metrics
Document and slide generation; Drive or Notion access if sources are connected
outcome: A complete campaign brief and concise team kickoff deck.

steps.title: Create the brief and deck
steps.prompt: Turn the attached strategy notes into a campaign brief covering objective, audience, main message, channel plan, timeline, and success measures. Follow the supplied brand voice. Clearly mark unanswered decisions instead of filling them with assumptions. Build a short kickoff deck that explains the brief and the decisions the team must make.

steps.title: Save the planning template
steps.prompt: Extract a reusable campaign-planning template and instructions from the approved brief. Include brand rules, required inputs, and the metric-selection framework.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Prepare the intake workflow
steps.prompt: Define a weekday workflow that detects new strategy-note files in [campaign folder] and creates a brief and kickoff deck in the matching campaign subfolder. List the file access and scheduling capabilities needed; do not claim it is running without them.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Turn user stories into interface concepts
summary: Translate real feedback into a mockup that fits the current product.
prerequisites: Provide user stories or feedback, relevant context, and design-system screenshots or Figma references.
outcome: A grounded UI mockup with a clear connection to the user problem.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Create a UI mockup that addresses [user story or feedback]. Read the supplied issue, discussion, and research context first. Identify the user problem, the intended outcome, and the constraints of the existing interface. Explore a concrete solution using the current design system, layout patterns, and reference screens. Explain how the main interaction resolves the problem and flag assumptions that need validation. Keep the concept tied to the evidence rather than adding unrelated features.

steps.title: Build a testable prototype
steps.prompt: Implement the selected concept as a focused interactive prototype. Reuse the current product patterns and test the primary journey, including its empty and error states, before proposing further scope.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Typeset handwritten course notes
summary: Convert equations and teaching outlines into consistent LaTeX course materials.
prerequisites: Readable photos of handwritten notes, topic outline, and syllabus
LaTeX generation and compilation capability
outcome: Editable LaTeX, a rendered PDF, and a matching practice sheet.

steps.title: Typeset the lesson
steps.prompt: Transcribe the attached handwritten integration notes and follow the supplied topic outline. Create a polished LaTeX lesson with accurate equations, consistent notation, and clearly distinguished definitions and examples. Flag ambiguous handwriting before deciding what it means. Compile a PDF and return the LaTeX source, checking that symbols and equation layout survived rendering.

steps.title: Improve learning navigation
steps.prompt: Add concise margin insights, a chapter overview, and visually distinct Quick Check boxes. Keep the visual hierarchy consistent and avoid overwhelming the equations.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

steps.title: Create matching practice
steps.prompt: Produce 15 integration-by-parts problems ordered by difficulty. Include a worked-format template showing where students choose u and dv while leaving the integration steps for them to complete. Match the lesson's notation and design.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after the preceding step.

title: Understand and extend an inherited spreadsheet
summary: Trace hidden dependencies before adding periods, commentary, and useful visual cues.
prerequisites: Upload the original workbook and any new actuals or assumptions.
Requires tools that read and preserve formulas, comments, formatting, and cross-sheet references.
outcome: An explained and extended workbook with preserved logic and a changelog.

steps.title: Explain before extending
steps.prompt: Read this workbook's legend, comments, formulas, and cross-sheet links. Explain how the tabs connect, how [key calculations] work, and which important assumptions are undocumented. Extend through [period] using the established patterns, add comments to complex logic, and include restrained trend visuals. Preserve existing formulas and identify any unresolved issue before changing its meaning.

steps.title: Verify the extension
steps.prompt: Create a changelog of added periods, formulas, and assumptions. Check reference continuity, totals, and selected input-to-output cascades. Incorporate these actuals: [data], then explain the forecast variance by supported drivers rather than an unexplained residual.

title: Validate a reserve workbook before drafting the filing
summary: Separate spreadsheet defects from reserve movements that need an actuarial explanation.
prerequisites: Provide the reserve workbook, prior filing, and methodology documentation.
Requires your organization's own NAIC data connector or supplied filings and bulletins; no generic NAIC connection is assumed.
Excel and Word editing tools are needed; the appointed actuary reviews and signs off the reserve judgments.
outcome: A cell-level issue brief, clean reserve walk, and draft filing narrative.

steps.title: Inspect the reserves
steps.prompt: Review [segment and period]'s reserve workbook, trace formulas across triangles and roll-forwards, and compare development factors and tail assumptions with prior filings and available bulletins. Separate broken formulas from genuine movements and judgment calls. Give exact sheet and cell references, the supporting calculation, and the likely effect of each issue before anything is changed.

steps.title: Reconcile and draft
steps.prompt: After these approved fixes: [list], rerun the reserve walk and test the supplied tail-factor range while holding other inputs fixed. Draft the methodology-change and reserve-movement narrative from the reconciled workbook, citing applicable requirements and flagging issues for actuarial review rather than declaring compliance.

title: Validate bulk RNA sequencing inputs
summary: Check reads, reference files, and sample quality before differential expression.
prerequisites: Provide sample sheet, FASTQ files, transcriptome and genome FASTA, GTF, and a configured bioinformatics runtime.
outcome: A run manifest, QC report, count matrices, and a clear downstream-readiness assessment.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Run a documented FASTQ-to-count quality review using [sample sheet], [FASTQ folder], and the supplied reference FASTA and GTF files. Validate inputs and compute resources before starting. Produce a run manifest, MultiQC report, and Salmon transcript- and gene-level count matrices. Interpret mapping rates, duplication, expected versus observed library type, and outlier samples. Separate warnings from issues that block differential-expression analysis, and link every concern to its sample and evidence. Return usable report links and the output paths.

title: Visualize a complex operating process
summary: Turn a long procedure document into a navigable view of decisions, owners, and paths.
prerequisites: Procedure or implementation playbook; volume data if flow widths should encode quantities
Interactive HTML rendering; optional Mermaid Chart connection
outcome: An interactive process diagram and editable source for team documentation.

steps.title: Map the process
steps.prompt: Read the attached implementation playbook and map the main paths, decision criteria, handoffs, and responsible teams. Build an interactive diagram with zoom and pan. Use a Sankey layout only where supplied volume data supports proportional flows; otherwise keep paths unweighted. Label branches by data readiness, integration capability, resources, and deployment readiness as supported by the document.

steps.title: Export an editable version
steps.prompt: Convert the process structure to Mermaid code for embedding in our documentation. If a Mermaid Chart connection is available, create an editable playground link; always return the raw source.
