title: Visualize program performance for stakeholders
summary: Make participation, satisfaction, completion, and learning outcomes understandable across programs and periods.
prerequisites: Provide program data as CSV or XLSX, metric definitions, time periods, and audience priorities.
Requires code, spreadsheet, and presentation creation; Drive is optional for supporting context.
outcome: A formula-driven dashboard and a concise visual board presentation.

steps.title: Build the visualization suite
steps.prompt: Inspect these program records for missing values, inconsistent definitions, and outliers before calculating results. Create an Excel dashboard comparing participation, completion, satisfaction, and pre/post learning measures by program and quarter. Then build an eight-to-ten-slide presentation emphasizing [audience priorities]. Use appropriate denominators, readable charts, and linked evidence; describe observed improvement without overstating causal impact.

steps.title: Add a meaningful comparison
steps.prompt: Break down [metrics] by [relevant demographic or location] where sample sizes support it. Research comparable benchmarks only if needed, document differences in definitions and populations, and add reference lines only when the comparison is defensible.

title: Write a business performance review
summary: Connect KPI changes and financial results into a source-backed leadership narrative.
prerequisites: Provide KPI definitions, close and forecast workbooks, prior reviews, and owner commentary.
outcome: An editable business review with cited numbers, anomalies, and owner questions.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Prepare the [period] performance review for [business or team] using only the supplied dashboards, financial tables, forecasts, prior review, and owner notes. Lead with the decisions and material changes leadership needs to understand. Explain key variances, anomalies, forecast changes, risks, and data-quality concerns with supporting charts where useful. Cite the exact source behind material figures. List missing inputs and unsupported explanations explicitly, and assign follow-up questions only where an owner is identified. Return an editable document for review.

steps.title: Audit the narrative
steps.prompt: Check every material number and causal explanation against its source. Mark unsupported claims, reconcile inconsistent figures, and tighten the leadership summary without concealing uncertainty.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Write a decision memo from research
summary: Compare evidence, alternatives, costs, and uncertainty in one reviewable recommendation.
prerequisites: Provide the decision, research sources, internal context, budget limits, and decision criteria.
outcome: A concise decision memo with traceable evidence and explicit tradeoffs.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Help [team] decide whether to [decision]. Use the supplied research, planning documents, models, stakeholder notes, and budget constraints. Apply [decision criteria] to the alternatives. Recommend a path with supporting evidence, costs, risks, tradeoffs, unresolved questions, and required owner confirmations. Keep any requested external research distinct from internal evidence. Link material claims to sources and record the assumptions that could change the recommendation. Produce a reviewable memo and supporting pre-read without making the decision or sharing it.

steps.title: Pressure-test the recommendation
steps.prompt: Argue the strongest evidence-based case for the leading alternative. Identify what new evidence or changed assumption would reverse the recommendation and revise the decision memo accordingly.
steps.instruction: Continue in the same conversation after reviewing the first result.

title: Write a PRD through a structured interview
summary: Clarify the user problem before drafting a specification in your team's format.
prerequisites: Provide the problem statement, PRD template, a strong past PRD, and research notes.
Connect Linear or Notion if supporting evidence lives there; document editing is needed for DOCX output.
outcome: A PRD with explicit goals, non-goals, success measures, and review questions.

steps.title: Interview and draft
steps.prompt: Before writing the PRD for [problem], interview me about affected users, current pain, constraints, and measurable success. Use our attached template and match the depth of the example PRD. Make goals and non-goals explicit, distinguish decisions from assumptions, and assign each open question to the appropriate design or product review.

steps.title: Check the scope
steps.prompt: Compare the draft with my interview answers. Flag invented decisions, goals without measures, and requirements that do not address the stated problem. Revise the PRD and produce a concise agenda for resolving its remaining questions.

title: Write an impact report grounded in program evidence
summary: Connect verified outcomes and financial stewardship with an authentic story for your stakeholders.
prerequisites: Provide participant, attendance, outcome, volunteer, finance, and qualitative-feedback records.
Requires data analysis, document creation, and chart generation; use only authorized participant stories.
outcome: A designed impact report with cited metrics, clear charts, and audience-specific versions.

steps.title: Build the report
steps.prompt: Analyze these records for [organization and reporting period]. First reconcile the key metrics, then create a report with an executive overview, program context, reach and demographics, outcomes, finances, and next-year goals. Use clear visualizations and only supplied, authorized stories or quotations. Separate measured outcomes from causal claims and flag incomplete data instead of inventing an impact narrative.

steps.title: Tailor the evidence
steps.prompt: Create three concise versions: one for funders emphasizing outcomes and cost-effectiveness, one for donors using verified human stories, and one for the board covering strategic implications and operational risks. Keep every number consistent with the approved report and show the source of each headline claim.

title: Write useful security review context
summary: Document the system boundaries and reporting rules reviewers need.
prerequisites: Provide architecture documents, repository instructions, security expectations, and known limitations.
outcome: A draft threat model and security policy grounded in the actual application.

steps.title: Start here
steps.prompt: Inspect [repository] and the supplied architecture material. Draft a threat model describing protected assets, entry points, untrusted inputs, trust boundaries, privileged operations, and authentication assumptions. Separately draft SECURITY.md guidance defining security invariants, reportable findings, severity context, and exclusions. Keep engineering workflow instructions in their existing home and link supporting documents as a knowledge base. Cite code or source evidence, mark assumptions for owner review, and include known limitations rather than inventing controls. Present the proposed documents before committing them.
